title_original: [Roadmap] Power Automate: AI-assisted UI Automation repair
excerpt_original: A new agentic debug run feature will be available in the flow designer. The UI automation repair interface launches while the flow is running, validating each selector used in the flow. It then proposes a new selector in case an existing one does not work as expected, after the user captures the respective element for reference. GA date: March CY2027 Preview date: July CY2026
title_ja: [提供予定・ロードマップ] Power Automate: AIを活用したUI自動化の修復機能
summary_ja: Power Automateのフローデザイナーに、AIを活用した新しいエージェント型デバッグ実行機能が追加されます。フロー実行中にUI自動化の修復インターフェースが起動し、セレクターの検証と、ユーザーの参照用要素取得に基づく新しいセレクターの提案を行います。
changes: フローデザイナーにエージェント型のデバッグ実行機能を追加
フロー実行中にUI自動化の修復インターフェースが各セレクターを検証
既存のセレクターが機能しない場合に新しいセレクターを提案

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilot app mode handoffs
excerpt_original: The Chat experience in the Copilot app will suggest a better-fit mode based on the user's prompt, if applicable. For example, it will suggest Cowork or other supported modes as they become available. Users will see a suggestion card after they send a prompt in Chat, with an explanation of the better-fit mode and an option for the user to switch to the suggested mode. Their chat conversation will be attached to the prompt in the new mode to maintain context. GA date: November CY2026
title_ja: [提供予定・ロードマップ] [ロードマップ] Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilotアプリモードのハンドオフ機能
summary_ja: Microsoft Copilotアプリのチャット体験において、ユーザーのプロンプトに基づいて最適なモードを提案する機能が追加されます。ユーザーは提案カードからモードを切り替えることができ、チャットの会話内容は新しいモードのプロンプトに引き継がれます。一般提供（GA）は2026年11月が予定されています。
changes: プロンプトに基づき、Coworkなどの最適なモードを提案するカードを表示
提案されたモードへ切り替えるオプションを提供
モード切替時もこれまでのチャット会話コンテキストを維持

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Viva: Insights and Copilot Analytics in DoD
excerpt_original: Microsoft Viva Insights and Copilot Analytics are coming to the Microsoft 365 Department of Defense (DoD) environment, providing eligible organizations with privacy-protected, role-based analytics experiences to help them understand Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption, usage, and impact. Viva Insights also provides data-driven behavioral insights into how employees collaborate, helping organizations improve productivity and wellbeing within the DoD environment. GA date: January CY2027
title_ja: [提供予定・ロードマップ] Microsoft Viva InsightsおよびCopilot AnalyticsのDoD環境への導入
summary_ja: Microsoft Viva InsightsとCopilot AnalyticsがMicrosoft 365のDepartment of Defense (DoD)環境に導入されます。これにより、適格な組織はプライバシーが保護されたロールベースの分析を通じて、Microsoft 365 Copilotの採用、利用状況、影響を把握できるようになります。また、従業員のコラボレーションに関するデータ駆動型の行動インサイトを提供し、DoD環境内での生産性とウェルビーイングの向上を支援します。
changes: Microsoft 365 Department of Defense (DoD) 環境向けに Microsoft Viva Insights および Copilot Analytics を提供開始
Microsoft 365 Copilot の採用、利用状況、影響を把握するためのプライバシー保護されたロールベースの分析機能を追加

title_original: Microsoft 365 Copilot release notes — October 27, 2026
excerpt_original: Updates released between October 13, 2026, and October 27, 2026. Microsoft 365 Copilot Learning Agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot [Windows] The Learning agent helps employees build skills through personalized microlearning and structured learning experiences. Roadmap ID: 490154 Details: What changed: Microsoft 365 Copilot now includes a Learning agent that helps employees discover personalized learning opportunities. The experience supports both microlearning content and structured learning paths, making it easier to find skill-building resources within the flow of work and upskill on Copilot. Why: Learning Agent makes continuous upskilling part of everyday work by delivering personalized, role- and task-relevant learning directly in Copilot. It helps employees discover what to learn, learn through real work, practice skills, identify gaps, and follow structured learning plans, enabling organizations to build AI fluency and role-based skills at scale. Try this: Open https://aka.ms/LearningAgent/add Click on any cards present on the home page or ask anything to learn/upskill Why this matters: Personalized learning guidance helps employees discover relevant training without extensive searching. Business impact: Organizations can support workforce skill development by helping employees find relevant learning resources more efficiently. Personal impact: Users can identify useful learning opportunities faster and spend more time building skills. Learn Learning Agent Overview of Learning agent Insights - New Copilot Metrics Available [Web] We are bringing a set of new Copilot metrics including actions taken in Microsoft 365 Copilot app, Edge and OneNote, and more key use cases across Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint including suggested reply, translate, coach, clean data and more. This will empower customers to more deeply understand the key Copilot adoption cases in Copilot Dashboard and Advanced Analysis in Viva Insights. Roadmap ID: 557981 Details: What changed: The update introduces detailed metrics for Copilot usage across Microsoft 365 apps including suggested reply, translate, coach, and clean data features. Previously, Copilot Analytics offered limited visibility into user actions and adoption patterns. This expansion enables tracking of Copilot interactions in the Copilot app, Edge browser, OneNote, and core Office apps, improving data granularity and security auditing capabilities. Why: Providing comprehensive usage metrics helps organizations understand how Copilot features are adopted and used, enabling better governance and optimization of AI assistance within Microsoft 365 environments. Try this: Open the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights. Navigate to Advanced Analysis to explore new Copilot usage metrics. Filter by application or feature to review adoption trends and user engagement. Why this matters: Detailed adoption metrics allow IT and business leaders to monitor Copilot usage effectively and make informed decisions about training and deployment. Business impact: Teams gain clearer visibility into AI tool adoption, supporting data-driven management of productivity tools and user experience improvements. Personal impact: Users benefit from tailored support and training based on actual Copilot usage patterns, reducing friction and increasing productivity. Learn: Microsoft Copilot metrics Microsoft 365 Copilot app Web Link as a Reference in Copilot Notebooks [Web] Add web links as references in your Copilot Notebooks. Roadmap ID: 516040 Details: What changed: Copilot Notebooks now support web links as reference sources. Previously, notebook references did not include web links based on the information provided. Users can add web content as a source when building notebook context for Copilot. Why: Relevant information often exists outside existing notebook sources. Adding web links broadens the information available to Copilot and helps users create notebooks with more complete context. Try this: Open a Copilot Notebook and add a reference. Paste a web link as a source for the notebook. Review notebook content and use Copilot with the added reference. Why this matters: Web-based sources can be included directly in notebook context, making it easier to work with information from multiple locations. Business impact: Teams can incorporate relevant web content into Copilot workflows without maintaining separate reference collections. Personal impact: You can bring useful online information into a notebook more quickly and reduce manual context gathering. New Copilot Notebooks design in the Microsoft Copilot App (iOS) [iOS] Copilot Notebooks in the Microsoft Copilot app (iOS) now lets users organize related chats, output creations, and references into a persistent AI workspace. Copilot uses the Notebook's accumulated context to ground responses, so work continues across sessions instead of starting over each time. Roadmap ID: 566318 Details: What changed: Copilot Notebooks in the Microsoft Copilot app on iOS provides a persistent workspace for related chats, generated content, and reference materials. Copilot uses the accumulated Notebook context to ground responses across sessions, reducing the need to re-enter background information. Copilot Notebooks in OneNote remain available, and notebooks in the Microsoft Copilot app can be opened as part of ongoing work. Why: The new Notebooks UX brings a lightweight, chat-first experience to the Microsoft Copilot app, making it faster to start work and easier to navigate while keeping chats, outputs, and references organized around a project or topic. Try this: Open the Microsoft Copilot app on iOS and create or open a Notebook. Add related chats, references, and generated content to the Notebook. Ask Copilot questions within the Notebook to use its accumulated context. Why this matters: A lower-friction experience in the Copilot app helps users quickly find and return to the context they need, stay in the flow of work, and continue in OneNote when they need the fuller workspace experience. Business impact: Teams can keep related AI-assisted work organized in a reusable workspace, improving continuity for ongoing projects. Personal impact: You spend less time reintroducing context and can resume work more quickly across multiple sessions. Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility User can use Canva Connector in Researcher [Web] User can use Canva Connector in Researcher. Details: What changed: Researcher now supports the Canva Connector. Previously, Canva content was not available through this connector within Researcher. Users can include connected Canva information as part of their research workflow in Microsoft Copilot. Why: This change expands the content sources available in Researcher. It helps users incorporate relevant Canva content without switching between tools. Try this: Open Researcher in Microsoft Copilot and start a research task. Select the Canva Connector if it is available in your environment. Review the returned Canva content and use it in your research results. Why this matters: Users can access additional connected content sources directly within Researcher, reducing context switching during research tasks. Business impact: Teams can incorporate Canva content into research workflows more efficiently when the connector is enabled in their environment. Personal impact: You spend less time moving between applications when gathering information for research tasks. Admins can create and deploy custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors across Microsoft 365 [Web] Admins can create custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors in the Microsoft 365 Admin Centre and deploy them across Microsoft 365. This will allow admins to surface their organization's custom data in Microsoft 365 Copilot via these MCP-based connectors. Roadmap ID: 501585 Details: What changed: Previously, admins had limited ability to integrate custom data sources with Microsoft 365 Copilot. Now, they can build custom MCP-based connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center and deploy them organization-wide. This enables Copilot to access and use proprietary data securely via these connectors. Why: This capability allows organizations to extend Copilotâs usefulness by integrating their unique data, improving relevance and decision-making while maintaining centralized control. Try this: Open the Microsoft 365 admin center. Go to the Copilot Extensibility section. Create a new MCP connector and deploy it to users across the organization. Why this matters: Custom connectors enable tailored Copilot experiences that leverage organizational data securely and at scale. Business impact: Teams gain enhanced insights by integrating proprietary data into Copilot workflows, improving collaboration and productivity. Personal impact: Users access richer, organization-specific information directly through Copilot, reducing time spent searching external systems. Rich entity representation for connectors in Search results [Web] Rich entity representation for connectors in Search results. Roadmap ID: 502533 Details: What changed: Search results in Microsoft Copilot now include detailed entity cards for connectors instead of plain text links. This update enhances visual context by showing metadata and relevant attributes directly in search results. It improves security by clearly identifying data sources and reducing misclicks. Why: Providing richer entity information helps users quickly understand connector content without navigating away, reducing errors and improving search efficiency. Try this: Open Microsoft Copilot and enter a search query. Review the connector results displayed with detailed entity cards. Click on a connector entity to access its full content with confidence. Why this matters: Clearer connector representations reduce confusion and help users find accurate information faster. Business impact: Teams benefit from faster data discovery and reduced risk of accessing incorrect connector data. Personal impact: You save time by identifying the right connector content at a glance without extra clicks. Work IQ APIs: Usage-based billing [Windows, Linux, Mac, Web] Enables usage-based billing for Work IQ endpoints, allowing developers to invoke agents and capabilities without requiring pre-assigned licenses, with usage billed based on the agents and models invoked per request. Roadmap ID: 559017 Details: What changed: Work IQ APIs now support usage-based billing, allowing developers to call agents and models without needing pre-assigned licenses. Previously, access required assigned licenses regardless of usage. Billing is now based on fixed or variable costs invoked per API request, improving cost transparency and flexibility. Why: This change removes licensing barriers for developers and aligns billing with actual usage, enabling more scalable and cost-efficient integration of Work IQ capabilities. Try this: Register your application to access Work IQ APIs. Invoke Work IQ agents or models through the API without assigning licenses. Monitor usage and billing based on the agents and models called per request. Why this matters: Developers can integrate Work IQ features more flexibly and pay only for what they use, reducing upfront licensing complexity. Business impact: Teams can adopt Work IQ capabilities incrementally without license management overhead, improving development agility and cost control. Personal impact: You can experiment and build with Work IQ APIs without license constraints, saving time on administration and reducing costs. Work IQ APIs - Endpoints: Declarative Agent Access [Web] Enables programmatic access to firstâparty and tenantâdefined declarative agents via the Work IQ endpoint, allowing applications to trigger specialized agents for domainâspecific tasks within broader workflows. Roadmap ID: 559019 Details: What changed: The Work IQ endpoint now supports programmatic access to both first-party and tenant-defined declara
title_ja: Microsoft 365 Copilot リリースノート（2026年10月27日）
summary_ja: Microsoft 365 Copilotの2026年10月27日更新では、パーソナライズされた学習を支援するLearning Agentや、アプリ利用状況を追跡する新たなCopilotメトリクスが追加されました。また、Copilot NotebooksでのWebリンク参照やiOSアプリでの新デザイン、ResearcherにおけるCanva Connectorのサポートが含まれます。さらに、管理者向けのカスタムMCPコネクタの作成・展開機能や、Work IQ APIにおける従量課金制の導入などが実施されました。
changes: 個人向けマイクロラーニングや構造化学習を提供する Learning Agent の追加（Roadmap ID: 490154）
Microsoft 365 アプリや Edge、OneNote における利用状況を追跡する新しい Copilot メトリクスの導入（Roadmap ID: 557981）
Copilot Notebooks における Web リンクの参照ソースとしての追加対応（Roadmap ID: 516040）
Microsoft 365 管理センターでのカスタム Model Context Protocol (MCP) コネクタの作成・展開機能の追加（Roadmap ID: 501585）

title_original: [Roadmap] Excel: Get and transform data with Copilot in Excel
excerpt_original: Get your data ready, just by asking. Describe the data you need and how you want it prepared, and the new get data skill handles the rest. It can connect and transform your data, then load the results into your workbook using Power Query, giving you a query you can inspect, edit, and refresh without having to build it yourself. Depending on the data source, authentication may be required. GA date: October CY2026
title_ja: [提供予定・ロードマップ] Excel：Copilotを活用したデータの取得と変換機能
summary_ja: Microsoft 365 Copilotの新機能により、自然言語で指示するだけでデータの取得や準備を行えるようになります。Power Queryを介してデータの接続と変換、ワークブックへの読み込みが自動で行われ、生成されたクエリの確認や編集、更新が可能です。
changes: 自然言語での指示によるデータの取得と準備
Power Queryを使用したデータ接続・変換・ワークブックへの読み込み
自動生成されたクエリの確認、編集、更新機能
データソースに応じた認証の必要性

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): App Blocks
excerpt_original: App Blocks enables M365 Copilot Chat users to turn their requests and data into rich, interactive experiences directly within the conversation, including calculators, dashboards, forms, planners, visualizations, simulations, comparison tools, and other interactive apps. It helps users move beyond static responses to explore data, adjust inputs, visualize outcomes, and simulate workflows in place, while supporting grounded scenarios where current information can be retrieved and then rendered into an interactive experience. GA date: October CY2026
title_ja: [提供予定・ロードマップ] Microsoft 365 Copilot: App Blocks機能
summary_ja: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chatにおいて、ユーザーのリクエストやデータを電卓、ダッシュボード、フォームなどのリッチでインタラクティブな体験へと変換する「App Blocks」機能が追加されます。これにより、ユーザーは静的な回答にとどまらず、データの探索や入力値の調整、結果の視覚化、ワークフローのシミュレーションを会話内で直接行えるようになります。
changes: リクエストやデータをインタラクティブなアプリ（電卓、ダッシュボード、フォーム、プランナー、視覚化ツール、シミュレーション、比較ツール等）に変換する機能を提供
静的な回答を超えて、会話内で直接データの探索、入力の調整、結果の視覚化、ワークフローのシミュレーションを実行可能
現在の情報を取得してインタラクティブな体験としてレンダリングする接地されたシナリオをサポート
target_user: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat ユーザー

title_original: [Roadmap] Excel: Edit with Copilot in Excel on iPhone
excerpt_original: Edit with Copilot makes it easier to edit and transform your Excel workbooks on your phone using natural language. Copilot can continue working on your task even when you move away from the app, so you can come back when the work is ready. Chat mode also remains available when you want to ask questions and get insights without making changes to your workbook. GA date: October CY2026
title_ja: [提供予定・ロードマップ] Excel: iPhoneでのCopilotによる編集機能
summary_ja: Microsoft 365 Copilotにより、iPhoneのExcelで自然言語を用いたワークブックの編集や変換が可能になります。バックグラウンド処理に対応しており、アプリを離れてもタスクが継続されるため、完了後に結果を確認できます。また、変更を加えることなく質問やインサイトの取得ができるチャットモードも利用可能です。
changes: 自然言語を使用したExcelワークブックの編集と変換機能の提供
アプリを離れてもバックグラウンドで処理が継続する機能
変更を加えずに対話やインサイト取得ができるチャットモードの利用

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): SharePoint Site Builder
excerpt_original: This feature enables users to easily create new SharePoint sites with Copilot. Users can review and confirm a clear site plan before Copilot builds the site. GA date: December CY2026 Preview date: October CY2026

Shared knowledge foundation : Agents can leverage common company-level knowledge while maintaining their own specialized sources, ensuring consistent answers across the organization. Supervisor oversight and governance : A centralized dashboard enables supervisors to monitor agent activity, reassign leads, and track the full qualification journey across all agents. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Envision and design AI agents in Business Central
excerpt_original: AI agents in Business Central Business Central introduces AI agents to help users automate repetitive tasks and make business processes more intelligent and efficient. These agents act as specialized assistants that understand context, handle structured data, and collaborate with users to complete end-to-end workflows. For example, the Sales Order Agent simplifies order creation by transforming natural language or email instructions into complete sales documents, while the Payables Agent streamlines vendor invoice processing by extracting key details from incoming invoices and matching them to purchase orders—all reducing manual effort and freeing users to focus on higher-value work. The agent runtime that powers these built-in agents provides core capabilities that enable the use of agentic AI within Business Central. AI agents are defined, configured, activated, and run directly inside the familiar Business Central environment—leveraging the same security model, administration tools, and user experience as the rest of the product. Results are displayed in-context, with intuitive navigation to related data and entities, allowing users to control the agents through the interface they already know. This consistency dramatically reduces the learning curve, builds trust, and ensures efficiency when working with AI agents. The agent runtime ensures that every step taken by an agent is traceable and operates strictly within the access boundaries (permissions) assigned during configuration. It provides a timeline view of all agent activities, allowing users to review what happened and why—enabling a true human-in-the-loop experience. The runtime can also memorize relevant data during execution, use it in subsequent steps, and request additional instructions in natural language when user input is needed. It helps ensure that sensitive operations always require explicit user review and consent, supporting full transparency and control. Business Central business processes are inherently multistep, stateful, and financially consequential. The agent layer must be able to interact with a broad set of ERP capabilities and data, sequence operations with a high degree of accuracy across dependent steps, handle the data respecting permissions, company, environment, and tenant boundaries, provide a contextual audit trail, and keep humans in the loop. Business Central agentic strategy intentionally separates deep, well controlled, in-context and transparent execution within the product from cross-system orchestration. Business Central agents form the foundational layer inside the product, exposing well-defined agent capabilities that in the future will be possible to surface as MCP tools and consume by Declarative Agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365. This layered approach enables Business Central-tuned, transparent, managed execution at the ERP core processes, while allowing higher-level Declarative Agents to orchestrate end-to-end business processes across products. Designing agents The new in-product experience for designing agents that automate Business Central processes is made available with AI Development Toolkit for Business Central. The experience offers a low-risk environment for envisioning and prototyping new AI agents tailored to your own business scenarios—extending the same agent runtime capabilities used by built-in Business Central agents. Built for rapid iteration, the designing experience lets you create and refine custom agents using natural language instructions, define their behavior, test agent profiles and permissions, and safely experiment with Business Central data in a sandbox environment. This approach empowers partner personas like consultants, product owners, and domain experts, as well as developers and even power users, to explore new scenarios, validate ideas, and build confidence in their agents before moving to production. Whether you aim to automate repetitive business processes, streamline data processing, or deliver proactive insights, the agent design experience gives you the tools to bring your vision to life. Agent instructions At the core of every agent are its goals and instructions, defined in natural language. Writing agent instructions is similar to writing prompts for large language models, so you can apply general prompt-writing best practices—and even use tools like Copilot to optimize them. The agent design experience includes a simple editor to help you define, refine, and test these instructions efficiently. Invoking your agent You can invoke your agent by manually creating a task for it. When doing so, you can include an additional message that provides specific details or context to complement the agent’s core instructions. Although the ability to design your own agents is in public preview, there aren't yet any built-in integrations to automatically trigger these custom agents based on incoming emails, events, or scheduled recurrences (this can be done by professional developers using the APIs available in the AI Development Toolkit). However, you can simulate these scenarios by including the email header and body in the task message to mimic incoming emails, or by manually triggering the agent to emulate event, UI action, or time-based runs. Troubleshooting When running the agent tasks in the designing experience, you can access detailed diagnostic views to help you understand and tune the agent execution. Since an agent’s decisions depend on its instructions, available data, and language model reasoning, you can review execution logs to see its inputs, reasoning process, and outputs. This helps you identify where uncertainty occurred and why specific decisions were made to adjust your agent instructions. Importing and exporting agents To make it easy to back up or move custom agents across sandbox environments, the in-product experience allows you to import and export agent definitions. These definitions are stored as simple JSON fil

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Run multiple Sales Order Agents per company with smarter item matching, relevance filtering, and streamlined setup
excerpt_original: You can now configure and run multiple Sales Order Agent instances in a single company. Each instance operates independently with its own mailbox, folder settings, email signature, and processing rules. Each agent instance tracks its own KPI metrics, such as emails received, quotes created, orders created, and time saved. The setup page is restructured to support per-instance configuration, and an upgrade path migrates existing single-instance setups to the new architecture. This change allows organizations to set up separate agents for different sales teams, product lines, or customer segments, each monitoring their own personal or shared mailbox. Improved items search: When a customer requests items, the agent now uses a multi-layer matching strategy: Exact identifier match: direct lookup by item number, vendor item number, GTIN, or cross-reference. Semantic attribute matching: extracts attributes from the customer's message (color, material, size) and ranks candidates by relevance using AI. Broader fuzzy search: falls back to a global item search when direct and attribute-based searches produce no results. Message and attachment relevance: The agent now validates incoming messages and attachments against a detailed relevance model before processing. Messages that fall outside the agent's responsibilities (such as offers to sell, requests for discounts, or attempts to extract internal information) are identified and filtered. A separate relevance check runs on attachments, ensuring that non-sales-related documents don't trigger unnecessary processing. The validation considers the full conversation history and the agent's defined scope to make accurate relevance decisions. Larger attachment files with diagnostics. The maximum number of pages per PDF attachment has been raised from 10 to 50, addressing customer feedback about the agent not reading larger purchase orders. A new cumulative content length limit of 150,000 characters is also enforced across all attachments in a single email (approximately 50K tokens). When an attachment is skipped, Business Central now stores the specific reason directly on the attachment record (page count exceeded, cumulative content length exceeded, attachment count exceeded, unsupported format, or analyze-attachments not enabled). This information is visible on the Attachments page and logged in telemetry, making it straightforward to diagnose why a particular document wasn't processed. Try it out. You can now create tasks for the Sales Order Agent without sending an email. From the agent's setup page, a new Try it out section lets you compose a message by selecting a sender (from your contact or customer list), entering message text, and attaching files. The agent acts like it received a real email. To help you get started quickly, two sample messages are included. One is a text-only message that references items from your catalog, and the other is a message with a sample purchase order attachment. The sample order is generated based on your actual item data, so the agent has realistic content to work with. These samples are particularly useful for first-time setup, demos, and testing agent behavior with specific scenarios without needing to send an actual email. Handling of unknown senders When the agent receives an email from an unregistered email address, you now have three options instead of just one: Create a new contact: register the sender as a new contact (existing behavior) Use another contact once: pick an existing contact from the contact list and link them to this specific task only, without modifying any master data. The override is stored per task message and does not affect future emails. Update an existing contact's email: select an existing contact and update their email address to the sender's address More control over email New configuration options give administrators more control over how the agent interacts with the monitored mailbox: Mark email as read: a new toggle to mark processed emails as read in the mailbox. This works in addition to the custom Processed by Sales Order Agent category, giving users a visual signal in their inbox. Mandatory folder selection: the agent now requires you to select a specific mailbox folder before activation. Previously this was optional and could lead to the agent monitoring an unexpected folder. If in doubt, choose Inbox . Stricter activation validation: trying to activate the agent without a mailbox folder now shows a clear error message instead of allowing activation in an ambiguous state. Prompts as embedded resources. The agent's AI prompts (instructions, item search logic, mail template checks, irrelevance validation) are now shipped as embedded resource files within the app extension package. This change reduces latency on first task processing and makes the prompt structure more transparent for engineering iteration. Business Value: The Sales Order Agent now handles more complex organizational structures and higher volumes with less manual intervention. You can run multiple agent instances in one company, each dedicated to a different team or shared mailbox with independent settings and performance tracking. The agent finds the right items more reliably by understanding product attributes, informal descriptions, and identifiers across multiple matching layers. The agent now processes PDFs up to 50 pages (previously, the limit was 10) and clearly shows why any attachment was skipped. It also filters irrelevant messages before processing, so credits aren't consumed by marketing emails or out-of-scope inquiries. If a customer writes from an unregistered email address, you can link an existing contact to that single task without creating duplicates. You can test the agent directly from the setup page without sending a real email, reducing the time to validate your configuration. Enabled for: Enabled for end users automatically GA date: July CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Copilot and AI innovation - Resolve customer emails autonomously with AI
excerpt_original: Autonomous email resolution delivers end-to-end handling of customer emails without manual intervention or default case creation. When an email arrives, the system analyzes the request, identifies the underlying intent, and determines whether the information and actions needed to resolve it are available. Using enterprise knowledge, configured business instructions, connectors, and custom agents, the system constructs a resolution dynamically. It generates a response that's context-aware, compliant with business rules, and tailored to the request, then delivers it directly by email—completing the interaction autonomously. If the customer isn't satisfied or the issue can't be resolved automatically, the system creates a case that carries the full conversation context, including customer intent, actions taken, and generated responses. A service representative can then step in without losing context or duplicating work. The capability is delivered through the Case Management Agent. An administrator enables the setting and sets the automation level for each line of business, from fully autonomous resolution to drafting a response for a service representative to review and send. This shifts email handling from a case-first workflow to an intent-driven resolution model, reducing manual effort, improving consistency, and accelerating time to resolution for high-volume customer interactions. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Use AI resources for your Copilot extensions
excerpt_original: Using the AI resources provides several benefits: Reduced operational overhead : Avoid the need to handle infrastructure management, updates, monitoring, troubleshooting, or maintenance of custom Azure OpenAI subscriptions. This benefit frees up resources to focus on core business operations and provides value-adding intellectual property (IP) to customers. Simplified onboarding : Quickly integrate AI capabilities into your solutions without having to navigate the complexities of setting up and managing your own Azure OpenAI subscription. Improved reliability : Proactive scaling, throttling, load balancing, and fault tolerance measures ensure consistent performance during peak demand. Enhanced security compliance : Built-in compliance measures and governance, including robust protection from malicious and harmful content, ensure compliance with data residency requirements. This benefit reduces the burden of ensuring regulatory compliance for ISVs. Streamlined experience for customers : Customers get a seamless AI resource management process without maintaining different configurations for separate ISV solutions. This capability also provides a cohesive AI consumption tracking and billing experience for Business Central customers. Customers who use AI resources across multiple AI-enabled solutions built with Business Central customer developer tools for Copilot benefit from a unified approach to AI consumption monitoring and invoicing. They don't need to reconcile multiple invoices or metrics from separate ISVs. For details on billing costs, see AI tools at Message scenarios . For most publishers, the default Business Central AI resources are enough. However, if you need specific models, including fine-tuned models, that the Business Central AI resources don't provide, you can bring your own subscription for customers. In this case, the publisher is responsible for deploying, maintaining, scaling, and securing the service. The publisher also handles billing AI resources to customers. We recommend using the developer toolkit AI resources when you extend Copilot in Business Central. You just need to authenticate with the SetManagedResourceAuthorization method in the AI Module AzureOpenAI codeunit. You also provide your own Azure OpenAI subscription details, but the authentication process doesn't use them. (Update 2026 release wave 1: There's now a new method signature for SetManagedResources that doesn't require you to provide your subscription details anymore. You should use that going forward.) // Example of using the default toolkit AI resources in AL AzureOpenAI.SetManagedResourceAuthorization(Enum::"AOAI Model Type"::"Chat Completions",AzureOpenAIAccountName,AzureOpenAIApiKey,AOAIDeployments.GetGPT4oLatest()); To use your own subscription, authenticate it with the SetAuthorization method. // Example of using your own Azure OpenAI subscription in AL AzureOpenAI.SetAuthorization(Enum::"AOAI Model Type"::"Chat Completions",GetEndpoint(),GetDeployment(),GetApiKey()); This AI billing model isn't designed to replace the existing Marketplace monetization pathway for publishers who create Business Central apps. Instead, it offers another option that simplifies AI consumption for customers and partners. ISVs can use the Marketplace monetization option to monetize their IP. Business Value: A key feature of the developer tools for Copilot in Business Central is that publishers in their Marketplace apps use large language models through Microsoft-managed Azure OpenAI resources when they extend Copilot in Business Central. This approach eliminates the need for customers to independently get and manage Azure OpenAI subscriptions. Using the Business Central AI resources is the default and recommended approach. However, some partners or customers might have special requirements that require them to use their own Azure OpenAI subscription when running the feature in production or when developing and testing in sandboxes, which is also supported in the developer tools for Copilot in Business Central. Enabled for: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically More info: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/ai-dev-tools-resources GA date: April CY2027 Preview date: June CY2025

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data: Agents and Copilot - Increase AI accuracy by grounding agents in customer insights
excerpt_original: The Customer Insights MCP server allows AI agents and chat experiences to access and understand insights generated by Customer Insights - Data. The Customer Insights MCP server uses the industry-standard MCP architecture to securely share unified profiles and insights with AI agents and chat experiences, providing the data context so AI agents can do their best work. AI tools can use the Customer Insights MCP server to: Resolve Dataverse contacts and leads to their unified customer profile. Access extended customer information unified by Customer Insights - Data from external sources not available to Dataverse. Understand calculated measures for a customer such as their purchase totals over the last 4 months, or the date of their most recent engagement. Quickly discover what segments the customer is a member of. See if a customer has multiple redundant contacts in your system, and which is considered authoritative for that customer. Get predictive insights for the customer such as Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) and Churn risk, giving you greater insights into the customer's current relationships with your company. Scenario Sally is a seller who is evaluating a lead named Joe who recently attended a product launch webinar. Sally asks her AI embedded on their Contact and Lead forms if there are any insights about this lead and is delighted to find that the lead Joe is matched to a VIP customer Joseph who has existing paid licenses for several products. Because Customer Insights - Data unifies her company's external Purchase and Rewards data with Dataverse contact and lead data, the agent informs Sally that Joe is a valued Rewards and Loyalty points member, and it is able to provide other AI-generated insights such as the Customer Lifetime Value score, Churn Risk, and the segments Joe is a member of. Armed with a wealth of customer data, Sally is able to engage Joe and upsell Joe on their new product. Business Value: Agents give your marketing, sales, and service teams essential insights and can automate many business processes. But agents are only as good as the data they work with. When you give them access to customer insights that unify your customer data sources, you can get more valuable and actionable insights that enable organizational efficiencies that you couldn't achieve before. Now, more insights generated by Customer Insights - Data can be leveraged from within Microsoft Copilot Studio, allowing you to turn insights into a powerful business asset. Copilot Studio, and even your own custom copilots created in Microsoft Copilot Studio, can now simply and easily get access to more insights, allowing agents to understand, share, analyze, and act on these insights. Every team member gets tailored information and tools to reach their goals efficiently. Enabled for: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically More info: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customer-insights/data/mcp-server-tools GA date: November CY2026 Preview date: June CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Administrator experiences - Use enhanced customer-first direct callbacks
excerpt_original: Customer-first direct callback introduces a configurable, AI-powered experience managed through "callback profiles" in the Copilot Service admin center. Administrators define a callback profile—including greeting message, alternate number capture, callback offering window, retry logic, and AI agent selection—and associate it with queues under overflow handling. For each queue where direct callback is chosen as an overflow action, the administrator also must select a callback profile to ensure a customized callback experience for the queue. Business Value: Customer-first direct callback gives you a smarter way to manage customer calls. Instead of making customers wait on hold, the system initiates a callback the moment they reach the front of the line, so that they never lose their place. A prebuilt AI agent captures callback details. You can use your own AI agent to run custom workflows like customer verification. Your representatives join the call only when the customer is ready, saving time, reducing missed calls, and boosting productivity. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Field Service: Optimize resource scheduling - Optimize schedules with Scheduling Operations Agent
excerpt_original: Dispatchers often spend considerable time and energy reviewing and adjusting each technician's schedule as conditions change throughout the workday: A technician has one or more cancellations in the afternoon. To fill the open slots, what requirements optimally keep promise windows, prefer high-priority work, and locate work around the same neighborhoods that the technician is due to travel to? A technician is running over the planned time for the current booking. As a result, they're late for the next booking, and the delay might cascade to subsequent bookings. How do you best adjust the bookings for the remainder of the day? A technician recovers from illness sooner than expected and is now available for work earlier than planned. What's the best way to schedule work for them when they return? A technician’s schedule contains a lot of low-priority work that isn't due for weeks. How can you improve the schedule with work that better meets desired business goals? A technician’s schedule for the day is built manually or with the schedule assistant. How can you rearrange the schedule so that the resource’s travel time is reduced? In each case, the dispatcher needs to assess the situation, determine which business goals apply, and then update the schedule manually, one booking at a time. With this release of the Scheduling Operations Agent, dispatchers can ask Copilot to provide the best schedule for the affected technician. Within seconds, the dispatcher gets a suggested schedule for review and can apply the updates. You can direct Copilot to optimize for the business goal you want, such as maximizing technician usage or work order priority. Copilot intelligently chooses among existing bookings and new unfulfilled work orders based on factors like skillset match, territories, and customer promise windows. Users can access the feature from the Copilot side pane anywhere within the Dynamics 365 Field Service application. Business Value: The Scheduling Operations Agent for Dynamics 365 Field Service enables dispatchers to quickly and easily optimize schedules for technicians as conditions change throughout the workday, so they can significantly improve their productivity. Dispatchers can ask Copilot to optimize schedules and address issues such as traffic delays, double bookings, or last-minute cancellations that often result in conflicts, gaps, or idle time in a technician's schedule. Instruct Copilot to achieve the desired business objective, such as maximizing technician usage or work order priority while considering factors like skillset match, territories, and promised time windows. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Unified routing - Orchestrate conversation distribution with natural language playbooks
excerpt_original: Conversation orchestration in Dynamics 365 Contact Center keeps every conversation actively managed throughout its lifecycle, from initiation through resolution. Instead of applying fixed rules at different stages of a conversation journey, conversation orchestration monitors each conversation as conditions evolve, like wait time increases, fast-filling queues, or service representatives going offline, and responds automatically with the right action. For example, administrators can define the intent using natural-language playbooks as follows: "If a premium customer waits for more than three minutes and no senior agents are available, increase their priority and offer a callback." Conversation orchestration then handles how it's run in real time. You can configure playbooks per scenario through guided templates that keep instructions focused and reliable. Built-in validation catches conflicts before anything goes live, so that you confidently publish changes without needing to test every edge case manually. The key capabilities are as follows: Dynamic priority escalation : In traditional systems, conversation priority is typically set once, at entry, and never revisited. This means a customer who has been waiting for 10 minutes competes for the same expert as another customer who has just arrived, and a conversation that’s transferred mid-journey resets to whatever the new queue's default priority is. Dynamic priority escalation fixes this by continuously re-evaluating priority as the conversation progresses. You define the conditions such as wait time thresholds, queue transfers, customer tier, or other context and conversation orchestration adjusts priority automatically throughout the conversation lifecycle. High-value or long-waiting customers move forward without anyone watching the queue manually. Overflow handling across multiple conditions : Conversation orchestration supports a broader set of business triggered overflow conditions, allowing organizations to respond intelligently as queue conditions change. Administrators can define actions when a queue is outside operating hours, when all representatives in a queue are signed out or unavailable, when queue wait time exceeds a defined threshold, or when the number of waiting conversations surpasses a specified limit. Depending on the situation, orchestration can automatically offer callbacks, route conversations to alternate queues, expand assignment eligibility, notify supervisors, or deliver contextual customer messages. This ensures customers are never left waiting without a defined path forward. Admins can also configure overflow handling for direct inward dial calls now, when reps are not available or don't accept the calls. Assign to a previously engaged or preferred representative : Customers often need to repeat information when they are connected to a new representative for every interaction. Conversation orchestration helps maintain continuity by reconnecting customers with previously engaged or preferred representatives whenever possible. Assignment decisions take into account historical interactions, queue membership alignment, representative availability, and workload capacity. For asynchronous conversations, organizations can choose to honor representative presence status and active conversation limits before reconnecting customers, ensuring returning conversations are assigned only when the preferred representative has capacity to engage. When the preferred or previously engaged representative is unavailable, conversations seamlessly fall back to the next best qualified representative. This reduces customer effort, improves resolution efficiency, and delivers a more personalized support experience. Bullseye routing : Finding the right representative often requires balancing expertise with response times. Bullseye routing enables organizations to gradually expand the pool of eligible representatives when a conversation isn't assigned within a defined timeframe. Administrators can define progressive routing rings that begin with the most qualified representatives and then expand to broader groups based on skills, proficiency levels, teams, or other business criteria. This approach maximizes the likelihood of connecting customers with the best-qualified representative while ensuring conversations don't wait indefinitely for a specific resource. These capabilities are the first in a broad and growing set of orchestration scenarios that conversation orchestration will support across the full conversation lifecycle, spanning overflow management, priority handling, assignment strategies, in-conversation messaging, and escalation. Each new capability builds on the same natural-language playbook foundation, so organizations can adopt new scenarios without rebuilding what they have already configured. Business Value: Traditional automatic conversation distribution systems rely on complex rules and static configuration that are difficult to maintain and can't adapt as conditions change throughout the conversation lifecycle. Unified routing with its new AI-powered conversation orchestration uses the power of agentic AI to continuously monitor events throughout the entire conversation lifecycle and responds with the right action when required. This is a shift from a static system to an orchestration layer that remains active and intelligent from the moment a conversation arrives in a queue until it's resolved. The new feature reduces administrative complexity and helps deliver more flexible customer experiences at scale, even under fluctuating demand. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users More info: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/contact-center/administer/configure-conversation-orchestration GA date: October CY2026 Preview date: April CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Journeys: Improve engagement and message timing with Outreach Optimization Agent
excerpt_original: Add the Outreach Optimization Agent to your journey, select the emails you want delivered, and let the agent handle timing and cadence automatically. With Outreach Optimization Agent, you can: Start with an intelligent baseline : Outreach Optimization Agent automatically creates a baseline messaging plan for your audience by analyzing overall historical engagement patterns, producing a smart, generic plan that is designed to work well for most customers before any individual optimization kicks in. Listen to incoming interactions and adapt the plan in real time : The agent continuously monitors incoming signals, including engagement and non-responsiveness, and adjusts follow-up timing and cadence, or exits the plan based on whether the goal is progressing or has been achieved. Respect quiet times : The agent enforces quiet time settings as a hard constraint, ensuring that messages are never sent outside approved communication windows, even if engagement data suggests otherwise. Scenario A global retail brand uses Outreach Optimization Agent in a seasonal campaign to re-engage customers. Unlike previous efforts with fixed schedules and repeated reminders, the agent creates a smart baseline plan, then adjusts message timing for each customer based on their engagement. It slows or stops follow-ups when customers show interest and spaces out reminders for unresponsive customers, all while respecting quiet times and consent. This leads to better engagement and less message fatigue, with minimal manual intervention. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Commerce: Author Commerce receipt formats with Copilot Cowork
excerpt_original: Use natural language in Copilot Cowork to create, update, translate, and check Commerce receipt layouts using existing formats in headquarters. The Commerce receipt format designer skill lets authorized users work with receipt layouts through natural-language requests in Copilot Cowork, using receipt configuration in Dynamics 365 Commerce headquarters. It applies to receipt formats used by Store Commerce point of sale (POS). Users can: Create and adapt formats: Start from an existing format in the modern Receipt designer representation, create a new format, or request changes to an existing target. Edit receipt sections: Modify header, line, and footer content, field positions, alignment, and supported formatting. Translate and personalize content: Translate static labels and add user-supplied text while preserving dynamic fields. Missing business details are identified rather than invented. Check layouts without changing them: Request structural or geometry checks that identify overlaps, width violations, and truncation risks, with findings and suggested remediation. Verify saved changes: Review the resulting format and changes, with saved configuration re-read to confirm the requested update. Creating a format from a source preserves that source. The skill is available automatically to authorized Copilot Cowork users. Users describe the source format and desired outcome, resolve any source or target ambiguity, and review the results. A Commerce administrator ensures appropriate headquarters access and that the source format is available in the modern structured representation. Structural checks do not establish visual appearance, barcode scanability, runtime values, or legal and fiscal compliance. Users review the layout in the Receipt designer and perform appropriate test printing before operational use. Assigning formats to receipt profiles or printers and printing or reprinting transactions are separate setup and operational workflows. GA date: December CY2026 Preview date: October CY2026

title_original: Visual Studio Code 1.143 — Copilot / Chat / Agents
excerpt_original:
Agents
Copilot harness as the default
The Copilot harness is now the default for new sessions in VS Code. It's our latest harness, built on the Copilot SDK, a shared foundation that helps align behavior, capabilities, and improvements across Copilot products.
When you start a new session, Copilot in the harness picker indicates that the session uses the Copilot harness:

In VS Code, you can keep Copilot harness sessions running in the background and access them from both the VS Code editor window and the Agents window. These sessions run through the Agent Host .
Thank you so much to everyone who has shared valuable feedback. This release includes more improvements shaped directly by your feedback.
We're continuing to improve performance and reduce latency based on the scenarios and setups you share. For example, reports of long waits before chat responses helped us reduce delays caused by MCP servers that don't finish loading their tools.
We're also continuing to make our documentation clearer based on the feedback and questions you've shared. Learn how to work with the Copilot harness , or explore the architecture and workflows in the agent host blog post .
Please continue filing issues to let us know how the Copilot harness is working for you. Your feedback is a huge help and directly shapes the harness experience.
Initial file-level working set support (Experimental)
Setting: chat.editor.workingSet.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders
You gave us feedback that when using the Copilot harness, approving or rejecting agent edits in the editor was challenging. As of this release, we are introducing initial file-level working set support to help you manage and review changes more effectively.
Copilot harness sessions in the editor window now support file-level Keep in the experimental working set above the chat input. Enable chat.editor.workingSet.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders to try it.
Select Keep on a file, or in the heading for all files, to mark changes as reviewed and remove them from the working set. The edits stay on disk, and files return if the agent changes them again.

What's next: We plan to add file-level Undo to the working set and bring Keep and Undo back into the editor for individual changes. These are planned for later releases, landing in Insiders first, then Stable.
Discard changes from more changesets in the Agents window
The Changes view in the Agents window lets you see all the modifications made by the agent. Until now, discarding pending changes was only available in the Uncommitted Changes changeset.

In this release, the Branch Changes , Session Changes , and Last Turn Changes changesets also offer the possibility to discard changes. Select Discard Changes on a file in the Changes view or in the multi-file diff editor. What VS Code discards depends on the changeset:
Branch Changes : restores the file to its version where the branch diverged from its base branch, and deletes files that the branch added. Session Changes : reverts the session's edits to the file and keeps changes made outside the session, such as your own edits. Last Turn Changes : reverts only the latest turn's edits to the file and keeps all other changes to it.
Compare model results (Preview)
Setting : sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders (Agents window only)
Compare how different models and harnesses approach the same coding task. Run attempts in parallel, review their results, and combine ideas into one solution.

To get started, enable sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders in the Agents window, then select Compare Models in the model picker.
Choose the approaches to compare: Select two or more models to attempt your task independently. You can mix Copilot, Claude, and Codex harnesses and configure different reasoning levels. Run the attempts: Enter one prompt and start all selected attempts together. Follow progress side by side: Each attempt runs in its own session, so you can compare its approach and open the worktree or changes at any time. Evaluate and combine the results: Optionally select a Judge model to evaluate the attempts and recommend a solution. Its scorecard shows time and token usage, with expandable rationale, validation evidence, and links to each attempt. You can then select Synthesize to build on the recommended attempt with ideas from the others. Synthesis starts only when you request it.
Tab shortcuts in an empty side pane
When you closed every tab in the Agents window side pane, the editor area was left blank, and you had to find the Add Tab (+) menu to get back to your session's changes or files.
The empty editor area now lists the tabs you can add, such as Changes , Files , Browser , and Search , each with its icon and keyboard shortcut. Select an entry to open that tab. If you have a canvas extension installed, a Canvas entry lists the available canvases. When you switch to a session whose editor area is empty, VS Code shows this list instead of reopening the Changes and Files tabs automatically.

Session Activity Bar (Experimental)
Sessions : sessions.showSessionActivityBar Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders , sessions.sessionActivityBar.showLayoutActions Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders
The Session Activity Bar brings a session's Changes , Files , Browser , and available canvases next to the side pane, keeping these editors and artifacts visually connected to where they open. You can still open session artifacts from the pills at the top of the session.
The Session Activity Bar is a slim vertical strip of icons at the right edge of the active chat. Select an icon to open that tab in the side pane. If the side pane is closed, it opens with that tab active. If the tab is already open, VS Code focuses it instead of opening a second copy. If you have a canvas extension installed, a Canvas entry opens a submenu of the available canvases.

You can drag the Session Activity Bar up or down by its grip to move it out of your way, and double-click the grip to reset its position. When you split the chat area, only the focused group shows the Activity Bar.
To keep session-related layout actions together, right-click the Activity Bar and select Show Layout Actions . This moves the Toggle Side Panel and Toggle Panel actions from the title bar into the Activity Bar.
The Session Activity Bar is off by default in Stable. Select View > Appearance > Session Activity Bar to turn it on. To hide it again, right-click the Activity Bar and select Hide Session Activity Bar .
You can also configure these options with sessions.showSessionActivityBar Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders and sessions.sessionActivityBar.showLayoutActions Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders . If you previously set sessions.showSessionToolbar , VS Code carries your value over to sessions.showSessionActivityBar Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders .
Find and create files from the empty Files tab (Experimental)
Setting : sessions.experimental.emptyFileEditorActions Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders
In the Agents window, the Files tab was blank when no file was open, so you had to switch to the Files view to find or create a file in your session's folder.
When you enable sessions.experimental.emptyFileEditorActions Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders , the empty Files tab shows a search box and a New File action. The search works like Quick Open ( ⌘P (Windows, Linux Ctrl+P ) ), with the same ranking, highlights, and file icons, and it only finds files in the folders of the current session. Select a result to open it in the editor, or select New File to create a file in the session's folder. When you close the file, the search box returns.

Improved performance when opening large chats
Opening a long Agent Host chat in the Agents window used to freeze the window for up to half a minute while the chat's history was restored. In this release, history is restored in small slices instead of one long blocking task, so the window stays responsive. Opening, switching back to, and reloading large chats is significantly faster.
Scenario Chat Time to open: 1.142 → 1.143 Window unresponsive: 1.142 → 1.143 Cold open Chat A (~1,150 requests, ~530 MB history) 35.6 s → 9.0 s 28.3 s → 0.6 s Cold open Chat B (~1,450 requests, ~200 MB history) 20.3 s → 3.0 s 20.3 s → 0.4 s Re-open Chat A 26.7 s → 0.6 s 26.8 s → 0.3 s Re-open Chat B 16.4 s → 0.4 s 16.4 s → 0.2 s Reload window Chat A 26.7 s → 2.9 s 25.3 s → 0.9 s Reload window Chat B 22.3 s → 2.2 s 20.8 s → 0.4 s
Median of three runs on macOS, with real chats from day-to-day development. "Cold open" means opening a chat for the first time after the window starts. "Re-open" means switching to another chat and back. "Window unresponsive" is the longest time the window could not respond to input during the open.
Reclaim storage from inactive worktrees (Experimental)
Setting : chat.agentSessions.sessionStorageCleanupSuggestion.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders (Agents window only)
Worktrees are very useful for letting agents work on multiple features simultaneously without interfering with each other's changes. Over time, inactive worktrees can accumulate and consume significant disk space.
Run Chat: Open Worktree Cleanup from the Command Palette to see how much disk space inactive agent session worktrees use and remove the ones you no longer need. Filter sessions by how long they have been inactive, review each worktree's size, and select the worktrees to clean up.
Cleaning up marks the selected sessions as done and deletes their worktrees. You can restore a session later to recreate its worktree. Active, running, needs-input, and pinned sessions are protected from cleanup.
The cleanup editor lets you configure automatic cleanup for sessions with merged pull requests and control whether VS Code suggests cleanup when session storage grows large.

When chat.agentSessions.sessionStorageCleanupSuggestion.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders is enabled, the Agents window notifies you when inactive worktrees accumulate or they use enough disk space to make cleanup worthwhile.


Chat
Open canvases from the chat menu (Preview)
Setting : chat.canvases.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders
VS Code 1.142 introduced canvases (Preview), which are shared, interactive surfaces for collaborating with agents.
In this release, you can now open available canvases from New Chat (+) > Canvas in the editor window, without asking Copilot to open them.

When canvas support is enabled and you have canvas extensions installed, the submenu appears after your first message in a Copilot harness session. You can also open canvases from the + menu in the Agents window.
Learn about installing, creating, and using canvases with the Copilot harness .
See output from detached background shells
In Copilot harness sessions, the agent can start commands that need to continue running after it responds in a detached background shell. A dev server or a file watcher are common examples of such commands.
Previously, you couldn't view the output of detached background shells, for example to check whether a dev server started successfully. Detached shells now stream their output like attached shells. Select the Background Shells pill, and then select a detached shell to watch its output as the command runs. The shell's terminal output in the chat response also keeps updating after the agent finishes its response. When the command exits, the shell leaves the list, and the chat response keeps the command's output and exit status.

You can now also stop detached shells, which was previously only available for attached shells . When you no longer need a dev server or watcher, select Stop Shell in the shell's details.

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Dataverse: Enable semantic data understanding for agentic use
excerpt_original: Give AI agents and Copilot a true understanding of your business data — not just raw schema — so they can answer questions accurately with less manual configuration. Learns from the systems you already run — Automatically extracts semantic knowledge from views, forms, and metadata already defined in your Dataverse environment, reducing agent deployment from days of manual setup to near-zero effort. Full visibility for makers — View generated semantic knowledge per entity — including name, description, and sample questions — directly in the Power Apps maker portal. Search for understanding gaps and enrich missing context with a built-in glossary for domain-specific terms. Governance and privacy built in — Enable or disable semantic signals at the org level, or at the individual signal-type or table level, giving makers and admins granular control to meet compliance and privacy requirements without sacrificing agent quality. No manual schema mapping. No custom query logic. No disambiguation between what your data is called and what your business actually means. GA date: November CY2026 Preview date: June CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Manage intraday operations with AI agent
excerpt_original: Intraday Agent is an autonomous AI agent that helps manage intraday operational scenarios. The following are its high‑level capabilities. Intraday queue tracking Continuously monitors queue volumes in real time. Detects anomalies when actual volume deviates significantly from forecasted demand. Automatically reforecasts in real time to assess current demand. Notifies supervisors with proactive alerts and recommendations. Automates corrective actions such as adjusting schedules, rescheduling breaks, or reallocating service representatives to maintain SLA performance. Supports customizable instructions to align mitigation actions with business needs. Intraday adherence tracking Monitors service representative adherence to scheduled shift activities in real time. Detects deviations such as late logins, extended breaks, or early logouts. Autonomously mitigates deviations through actions such as break rescheduling, shift extensions, overtime activation, or flexible channel reassignment. title_original: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.100
excerpt_original: 2026-10-19 - Add --disable-client-telemetry flag to turn off client telemetry uploads from the CLI - Add --trust-folder for one-off prompt-mode sessions started with -p or piped stdin - Install verified Skills and plugins from GitHub install links via copilot plugin install "ghapp://air/install?..." - Open /share without arguments to view a full-screen action menu for sharing the current session - Sandbox host-rule traffic now honors HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY when no sandbox proxy is configured - Voice dictation no longer inserts language markers like <en-US> into transcript text - Managed plugins update activation in existing sessions when managed policy changes - Sessions no longer stall for minutes when an MCP server hangs while loading tools. - Gemini tool calls no longer fail when array parameters define enum values - Gemini chats no longer fail after earlier tool results contain no readable content. - Sandboxed shell commands now explain credential-proxy certificate trust failures and can offer an approved rerun outside the sandbox. - Keep saved /diff review comments when reopening an unchanged diff in the same session, with an explicit discard action. - Plugin enable, disable, update, and uninstall actions now route reliably after plugin inventory refreshes. - Reasoning-only max-token responses no longer loop indefinitely and now end with a clear error when no progress is made - Show a clear warning and keep the active model display in sync when a saved model is automatically replaced on resume. - Sandboxed commands on Linux start more reliably without intermittent loopback setup failures - Back from MCP resource details stays on the list during live metadata refreshes - Native chats can start and finish while optional managed plugin downloads continue in the background. - Double Ctrl+C exits immediately even when the CLI UI is busy - Catalog search reports proxy authentication requirements for CONNECT proxy challenges - HydraFusion keeps a pass expanded while its review runs, passes that were not kept stay expandable until you switch sessions or resume, and passes from an aborted turn say whether they were kept - Managed account policy and bypass-mode warnings stay accurate after switching accounts, even when a policy cache miss happens. - Avoid false context exhaustion and rollover refusal when tool definitions are deferred - Custom agents that declare the documented `search`, `web` or `todo` tool aliases, or name `github-mcp-server/web_search`, now receive the matching tools - CLI help and version flags exit reliably after printing their output - Enterprise-managed ask permissions in Assisted mode now allow safe actions without unnecessary confirmation prompts. - Keep your selected Microsoft Entra account pinned during sign-in and token renewal - Up from sessions sidebar header actions wraps to the last visible session - Plan, autopilot, and shell mode badges stay visible while startup components load and the agent works. The badge replaces the mode suffix that used to trail the activity text (`Working - plan`), and the startup `Loading:` row now truncates its diagnostics to keep the status row on one line - Sandboxed commands can write package and build caches when developer tool access is enabled. - Windows CLI Git commands now recover from thread-access-denied startup failures. - A skill `allowed-tools` rule keeps commas inside its arguments instead of being split apart. Where a list's structure is ambiguous, its unscoped rules now prompt instead of being granted. - MCP resource dashboard stays interactive while inventory adapters refresh - Retry image-bearing Responses requests with smaller payload limits when providers reject oversized bodies - Complete usage reporting no longer shows partial status or phantom unattributed spend after resume when billing data is complete. - Assisted permissions send nested PowerShell and bash -c commands that only expand plain-data environment variables, single-quoted PowerShell, and PowerShell variable and alias statements to the permission judge instead of requiring unnecessary manual approval - Path-specific instruction files in the repository root .github/instructions are now applied automatically when the agent reads or edits a matching file - Start git, shell commands, and MCP servers on Windows when process snapshot thread enumeration fails - Use the unified Sessions browser by default for /sessions, /session, and /resume. - Session browsing now caps account discovery at 500 records and respects Retry-After hints for automatic refresh timing. - Prompt to update the sandbox proxy certificate authority when masked hosts change - Show a clear notice when administrator-managed settings override your selected model - Enable semantic code search by default for online sessions. - Improve /login for Microsoft Entra by letting you choose a cached account or explicitly sign in with a different account - Sandboxed git on github.com can use your configured GITHUB_TOKEN from credentials.envVars - /sandbox can keep sandboxing enabled for the current session without enabling it globally - Trusted repository plugins install and update automatically before chat runs. - Rename the built-in browser plugin to browser-use and keep existing browser plugin preferences working after upgrade - Sandbox allows local network access by default so commands can reach localhost and private-network services.

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Field Service: Optimize resource scheduling - Optimize multiple resources with Scheduling Operations Agent
excerpt_original: This release expands the optimization capabilities of the Scheduling Operations Agent to include multiple resources. The agent considers the availability of the resources, their current schedules, and unscheduled requirements. It suggests a schedule that honors configured constraints and optimizes it according to the selected goal. Dispatchers can review and compare the proposed schedules with the current schedules before applying changes. New capabilities include: Optimize schedules for up to 5 resources directly from the schedule board. Optimize schedules for up to 30 resources using an optimization plan. Create custom goals and weight objectives. Create custom optimization scopes to use with your optimization plans. These capabilities build on the existing public preview of the Scheduling Operations Agent and will be automatically enabled for all organizations that have the agent enabled. Learn more at Scheduling Operations Agent documentation . Business Value: Optimize multiple resources with the Scheduling Operations Agent (SOA). Schedule up to five resources directly from the schedule board or Copilot or perform ad-hoc optimizations for up to 30 resources using an optimization plan. This feature streamlines scheduling, improves efficiency, and supports better resource management. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users More info: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/field-service/soa-overview GA date: March CY2027 Preview date: June CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Reporting and data analysis - Use new APIs for analyzing approval workflows for auditors and IT staff
excerpt_original: In this release wave, we're introducing read-only APIs on the (workflow) approval system. This allows for establishing security and auditing analytics and reporting outside Business Central—for example, creating reports with Power BI or agents with Microsoft Copilot Studio and MCP Server for Business Central. The APIs are read-only and allow querying for: Workflow Workflow and User mappings Workflow, User, and Action history We're also introducing a new permission set that allows a user to use approval APIs. This shouldn't be granted to standard users, but might be included in security-related permission sets. Business Value: This feature enhances transparency and control by enabling secure, read-only access to approval workflows and user actions. Businesses can leverage these APIs to build advanced auditing and compliance reports in tools like Power BI, ensuring stronger governance and accountability. Additionally, integration with Microsoft Copilot Studio and MCP Server opens opportunities for intelligent automation and analytics, driving efficiency and insight. By isolating permissions for API access, organizations maintain robust security while empowering authorized teams to innovate confidently. Enabled for: Enabled for end users automatically GA date: June CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Filter the adherence tracker by planning group
excerpt_original: This feature provides the following capabilities: The adherence tracker includes a planning group filter that supervisors can use to scope the view to a specific planning group. The planning group filter works with the existing shift plan and service representative filters, so supervisors can combine filters to refine a single view. The tracker displays representatives based on the planning groups associated with their scheduled shifts. This behavior keeps the tracker aligned with the shift plan used to calculate adherence. The tracker saves each supervisor’s filter selections across sessions and opens with their previous scope. The tracker recalculates adherence percentages and out-of-adherence counts for the filtered scope, providing a planning group-level view of intraday adherence. In Copilot Service workspace, go to Workforce management > Adherence tracker . Access and prerequisites To use Workforce Management capabilities, an administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from the Power Platform admin center. Business Value: Supervising large contact centers is tough when you have to scan endless lists to find your team. Now, with planning group support, you can filter the adherence tracker to just the groups you manage. That means you spot issues faster and act right away, keeping service levels on track in real time instead of fixing problems after the fact. This feature scales for enterprise operations with hundreds of representatives and aligns with the same planning group structure you already use for forecasting, staffing, and scheduling. It saves time, reduces complexity, and helps you stay focused on what matters most: delivering consistent service. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users GA date: August CY2026

summary_ja: Dynamics 365 Customer Serviceのワークフォースエンゲージメント管理において、アドヒアランス トラッカーにプランニンググループフィルター機能が追加されます。スーパーバイザーは特定のプランニンググループで表示を絞り込み、既存のシフトプランやサービス担当者フィルターと組み合わせることが可能です。設定されたフィルターはセッション間で保存され、フィルタリングされた範囲に基づいてアドヒアランス率や例外件数が再計算されます。
changes: アドヒアランス トラッカーにプランニンググループフィルターを追加し、特定のグループに表示を限定することが可能に
既存のシフトプランおよびサービス代表者フィルターとの組み合わせや、セッション間でのフィルター選択の保持に対応
