title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Filter adherence historical analytics by planning group
excerpt_original: This feature provides the following capabilities: The adherence historical analytics report includes a planning group filter that workforce managers can use to scope results to one or more planning groups. The planning group filter works with the report’s existing filters, allowing managers to combine planning groups, date ranges, and other report parameters in a single view. The report recalculates adherence metrics for the filtered scope, providing a group-level view of adherence performance instead of a contact center-wide aggregate. The report associates representatives with planning groups through their scheduled shifts. This behavior keeps historical reporting aligned with the shift plans used to calculate adherence. Planning groups must be configured and have assigned representatives before the filter returns results. In Copilot Service workspace, go to Workforce management . Access and prerequisites To use Workforce Management capabilities, an administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from the Power Platform admin center. Business Value: Adherence only matters when it reflects how your work is organized. Until now, historical adherence reports didn’t account for planning groups, making it hard to see if performance dips came from a single under-supported queue or were spread across the operation. With planning group support, you can focus your analysis on the groups that matter and compare adherence across them for the same time period. This gives you clearer insights and helps you make smarter staffing decisions. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users GA date: August CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Copilot and AI innovation - Use Copilot Cowork to orchestrate insights and actions for representatives
excerpt_original: The plugin in Copilot Cowork is available out of the box for service representatives. They can use the Customer Service skills after the administrator enables the plugin for them in Cowork settings. The key capabilities are as follows: Prioritizes and enriches cases : Surfaces highest-attention cases with suggested next actions. Reviews for criticality and severity : Flags cases where severity mismatches actual urgency signals. Briefs case at intake : One-screen customer, history, prior cases, and SLA snapshot. Summarizes root cause and resolution : Proposes likely cause and ranked next-step resolutions. Matches knowledge articles : Matches top articles, flags gaps, updates stale content. Drafts replies : Generates template-based customer email replies for CSR review. Handles escalations and handoffs : Detects triggers and assembles escalation packet for next owner. Business Value: The Customer Service plugin in Copilot Cowork helps service teams boost productivity at scale by offloading complex, multi-step case workflows. It ensures every action is grounded in the right Dynamics 365 environment and enriched with Microsoft 365 context, eliminating manual lookup. The custom skills allow teams to tailor Cowork to their workflows, knowledge sources, and triage rules for more precise assistance. The built-in checkpoints provide human-in-the-loop governance, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and trust before any changes are committed. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users GA date: June CY2026 Preview date: May CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Sales: Copilot and AI innovation - Use Dynamics 365 Sales skills in Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork
excerpt_original: As an admin, you can control who can access Copilot Cowork in your organization. The Dynamics 365 Sales plugin is installed by default in Copilot Cowork and available to all users who have access to Cowork. As a seller, you can use the sales skills in Copilot Cowork to: Understand customer, opportunity, and pipeline context without manually gathering information from multiple systems. Identify changes, risks, engagement patterns, and areas that require attention. Prioritize work across customers, opportunities, leads, and pipeline activities. Generate recommendations and next-best actions based on available business context. Analyze business performance, pipeline health, and sales execution trends. Support decision-making across individual, team, and organizational sales workflows. Business Value: If you spend the day moving between CRM, email, meetings, calendars, and collaboration tools, Dynamics 365 Sales skills bring that context together in Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork. By grounding Cowork in Dynamics 365 Sales data and Microsoft 365 signals, you get more relevant insights, recommendations, and actions in the flow of work. This helps you quickly understand customer relationships, opportunity health, pipeline changes, and next steps, so you spend less time gathering information and more time moving deals forward. By combining customer, opportunity, account, lead, activity, and pipeline information with emails, meetings, calendars, and collaboration signals, Cowork can help users understand what has changed, identify what requires attention, and determine appropriate next actions. Enabled for: Enabled for end users automatically More info: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/use-copilot-cowork-sales-skills GA date: June CY2026 Preview date: May CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations cross-app: Boost productivity with Copilot - Use Copilot Cowork to orchestrate insights and actions across Dynamics 365 ERP
excerpt_original: The Copilot Cowork plugin for finance and operations apps enables users to move from business intent to insight to execution in a single experience. Copilot orchestrates work across ERP data, emails, documents, spreadsheets, collaboration tools, and downstream business processes. Key capabilities Orchestrate workflows across ERP and Microsoft 365 data sources. Analyze business data and generate contextual insights. Reason across finance, operations, and supply chain domains. Generate recommendations and prepare next steps. Execute actions while keeping humans in the loop. What this means for customers The value is not just accessing ERP data through AI. Copilot Cowork enables agentic workflows where it can reason over business context, gather relevant information, evaluate options, and generate recommended actions. This reduces manual coordination across systems, accelerates decision-making, and improves consistency in how business processes are executed. User experience shift Users can interact with ERP through business intent rather than navigating complex application layers and disconnected tools. This creates a more natural way to work, where users focus on outcomes instead of system interactions. Preview scope Initial set of scenarios across finance and supply chain. Limited action coverage for transactional workflows. Available to selected preview customers. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Unified routing - Use pick-based assignment method for work items
excerpt_original: Use the No auto assignment method for queues in Copilot Service admin center when you want routed conversations to remain unassigned after they enter a queue. Instead of being assigned automatically, conversations stay in the queue until a service representative picks them up from their Inbox or a supervisor assigns them manually. This assignment method supports a pick-based work distribution model, giving supervisors and service representatives greater control over how work is handled. Unlike the push-based model used by other out-of-the-box assignment methods, which automatically assign conversations based on representative availability and capacity, the no auto assignment method allows teams to review incoming work and decide who should handle it. This approach is well suited for organizations that prefer manual oversight, specialized work selection, or supervisor-managed assignments. Business Value: Improve operational control and consistency by enabling service representative-led work distribution. Conversations remain available in the queue until manually assigned by supervisors or picked by representatives, helping teams handle specialized, regulated, or sensitive interactions effectively. excerpt_original: This feature enhances Dynamics 365 Project Operations by extending its native work breakdown structure effort tracking to include approved time captured in Field Service when the Field Service and Project Operations integration is enabled and time flows in at the project task level. Approved Field Service time now contributes directly to task-level WBS execution metrics in Project Operations when time is captured against a project task. Task metrics such as effort completed, effort remaining, percent complete, estimate at completion, and schedule variance are calculated using approved field labor under the same native project rules used for time entered directly in Project Operations. Because these calculations occur at the leaf task level, their impact rolls up automatically to summary tasks and the project root. Effort tracking views, reprojections, and project-level status indicators reflect real execution in the field, rather than inferred progress or manual reconciliation. Project managers can assess delivery health, forecast outcomes, and identify schedule risk using execution metrics grounded in approved field work. This enhancement doesn't introduce new execution logic or formulas. It enables existing Project Operations WBS effort tracking behavior to include Field Service execution when time is captured against project tasks. This feature is only available when the Field Service and Project Operations integration is enabled. Business Value: When field technicians complete work tied to a project task, you see that progress reflected immediately in your project health metrics. Approved Field Service time flows directly into task-level work breakdown structure (WBS) tracking in Dynamics 365 Project Operations, so effort completed, percent complete, estimate at completion (EAC), and schedule variance stay accurate without manual reconciliation. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Speed up processing with Known Senders in Payables Agent
excerpt_original: This feature introduces email review policy and a Known Senders list page to give accounts payable teams more control over which incoming emails require human approval before the Payables Agent processes them. A new Email review field in the Payables Agent setup lets administrators choose when incoming emails require human approval. The following options are available: Always: Every email requires approval, regardless of the sender. Never: No emails require approval. Only if untrusted (recommended): Only emails from senders who aren't on the list of known senders require review. This is the recommended setting for most organizations. Administrators must explicitly select an option before they start to monitor the email inbox. To ensure that they make an active decision, a default isn't preselected for the field. Every known sender is subject to a setting that sets the review policy for the specific sender. When you set the email review policy to Manage per sender , the agent evaluates incoming emails in the following order: Invoice is uploaded and not received via email: No review required. Email subfolder is configured: All emails in the monitored subfolder are treated as trusted. No review required. Sender is on the Known Senders list: Action depends on the configured value (Ask, Approve, or Reject). Internal sender (same organization, not on the list): No review required. Internal detection uses email authentication headers (planned to be available in 2026 wave 2, version 29.0.). Administrators can maintain a list of known senders, each with a configured policy: Ask: The email requires human approval. Approve: The agent processes the invoice without review. Reject: The sender is blocked and the attachment isn't processed. To build the list organically, after you review an email and want to continue, the sender is added automatically to the list of known senders, provided that the Manage per sender policy is active. Security telemetry is logged for each auto-addition. This feature is available from the August minor release of 2026 release wave 1. Business Value: Payables Agent processes vendor invoices received by email, but today every incoming email requires supervisor approval before the agent can act on it, unless email review is disabled entirely. This creates friction for accounts payable teams who repeatedly receive invoices from the same vendors. They must manually approve each email, even from senders they already trust. The Known Senders feature lets businesses define which senders the agent can process automatically, reducing manual intervention while maintaining control over unknown or unverified sources. With this capability, organizations can safely default email review to off, moving closer to fully autonomous invoice processing. Enabled for: Enabled for end users automatically GA date: August CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Try Payables Agent for free without setting up email
excerpt_original: Payables Agent introduces a free trial mode that any user can start without help from an administrator or having paid credits. You can start the trial directly from the agent setup card or from the Purchase Invoices page. You don't need to have an administrator role or configure an email account. You upload invoice PDFs manually to start processing, bypassing the email-based sourcing flow entirely. The trial activates immediately the first time you upload an invoice. The trial includes 50 free invoice uploads. Each upload counts against the quota. You can track your remaining quota on the agent setup card throughout the trial. The full agent workflow is available during the trial: Extract invoice data Match vendors Suggest lines Create and finalize purchase invoice drafts You can experience the same capabilities that you would after subscribing. If you use up your quota of 50 invoices, continued use requires available credits. This feature is available from the May minor release of 2026 release wave 1. Business Value: Trying out the Payables Agent currently requires that you configure an email connection, which is a step that creates friction before a user has even seen what the agent does. Accounts payable clerks and accountants who want to explore the agent often can't do so on their own, because setting up email often requires help from an administrator. This feature lets any user start a Payables Agent free trial by uploading invoice files directly, with no email configuration required. Companies get a quota of 50 free invoices to experience the full agent workflow, including data extraction, vendor matching, line suggestion, and draft creation and finalization. By removing the technical barrier and the need to involve an administrator, more users can discover the agent's value firsthand and build the case for adoption within their organization. Enabled for: Enabled for end users automatically GA date: July CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Copilot and AI innovation - Classify emails by category and subcategory with Case Management Agent
excerpt_original: With email classification, administrators can define a custom taxonomy of categories and subcategories to automatically classify inbound emails in Dynamics 365 Customer Service. AI analyzes the email subject and body, then stores the assigned category or subcategory on the email activity record. Case Management Agent, automatic record creation rules, Power Automate flows, reporting, and other downstream processes can use this value to determine how to handle the email. Administrators can enable email classification and define category and subcategory names and descriptions. They can also set conditions that determine which emails are classified, such as specific mailboxes, sender domains, languages, and so forth. When the feature is enabled, the system qualifies inbound emails and automatically classifies them by using the Case Management Agent flow. Administrators can also manually update an assigned category or subcategory, or disable classification to stop processing new emails. Business Value: Email classification gives you control over how incoming emails are managed before any action is taken. It automatically sorts messages so you can ignore irrelevant ones, let the Case Management Agent handle routine issues, and focus on those that truly need human attention. This reduces clutter from non-support emails like thank-you notes, newsletters, and spam, allowing both AI and your team to concentrate on what matters most. The result is time saved, lower processing costs, and the ability to scale automated email handling confidently without adding operational risk. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users GA date: August CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Omnichannel customer experiences - Handle duplicate callback requests in overflowing queues
excerpt_original: In the in-queue and pre-queue overflow settings within the Copilot Service admin center, administrators can define the following settings: Prevent duplicate callback requests from the same phone number. Define deduplication logic using combinations of caller phone number, channel phone number, and queue ID. Configure caller experiences when a duplicate is detected. An option to end the call or play a custom message in a loop is available. For example: “You are already in queue to receive a callback when a customer service representative is available. Your latest wait time is 12 minutes. You can choose to continue waiting on this call if needed or disconnect and receive the callback.” Specify the phone number to initiate the callback from. Business Value: This feature delivers significant benefits by enhancing customer experience, operational efficiency, and administrative control. It prevents redundant callback requests from the same phone number, reducing unnecessary loads on representatives and systems. Administrators gain flexibility to configure deduplication logic and tailor the caller experience, including custom messaging when duplicates are detected. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Detect intraday volume spikes with workforce alerts
excerpt_original: Supervisors can create volume spike alerts that compare real-time conversation volume with the forecast linked to a shift plan. When volume remains above forecast for the configured number of intervals, selected recipients receive an in-app notification. The capability includes the following features: Administrators can enable workforce alerts in Copilot Service admin center by going to Workforce management > Intraday management > Workforce alerts . Supervisors can create and manage alerts from Workforce alerts in the Copilot Service workspace site map. Each alert references a shift plan and monitors the queues associated with its linked capacity plan. Supervisors can specify the percentage by which actual volume must exceed forecast volume. Supervisors can specify the number of consecutive intervals during which the deviation must continue before an alert is raised. The forecast determines whether an interval is 15, 30, or 60 minutes. Supervisors can set an expiration date to limit an alert to a campaign, season, or known event. Supervisors can select one or more notification recipients for each alert. Active alerts are evaluated on a recurring schedule. Notifications are sent when the configured threshold and duration are met. Recipients can select a notification to open the alert details. The details include the queue and alert name, detection time, current and forecast volumes, spike percentage, and an interval-by-interval breakdown. Access and prerequisites An administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from Power Platform admin center. Forecasting and scheduling must be configured. The selected shift plan must have a linked capacity plan and forecast. Real-time conversation data must be available for the monitored queues. Business Value: Contact centers plan staffing based on forecasted demand, but actual demand can change quickly. When conversation volume rises significantly above forecast, queues can grow and service levels can decline before supervisors have time to respond. Workforce alerts help supervisors identify unusual intraday volume changes without continuously monitoring a dashboard. Supervisors define the deviation and duration that represent a volume spike and select who should be notified when those conditions are met. The notification provides information about the spike, including how far actual volume is above forecast and whether the deviation is continuing. Supervisors can use this information to decide whether to shift capacity, offer overtime, or defer offline work while these actions can still help protect the customer experience. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users More info: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/contact-center/use/workforce-management-use-volume-spike-alerts GA date: October CY2026 Preview date: August CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Unified routing - Handle waiting conversations when queues close or become unstaffed
excerpt_original: This capability enhances queue handling by intelligently detecting two key scenarios where conversations would otherwise remain unserved: Queue transitions to out-of-operating hours : The system continuously monitors active conversations that entered a queue before closing time. If the queue transitions to out-of-operating hours while conversations are still waiting, it automatically applies admin-defined overflow actions. Customers can be guided to leave a voicemail, request a callback, or be transferred to another available queue, ensuring a smooth end-of-day experience without manual intervention. No service representatives are signed in : The system evaluates real-time representative availability. If all representatives assigned to a queue are signed out, it immediately triggers the configured fallback action instead of waiting for in-queue overflow timers. This is especially valuable in scenarios such as mass logout events, unexpected breaks, or holidays not captured in operating hours. Administrators configure both scenarios using natural language prompts in conversation orchestration, enabling fine-grained control over queue behavior. This ensures customers are always routed to the best possible outcome, even when direct support is unavailable. Business Value: This capability ensures customers are never left waiting when representatives aren't available. Whether a queue transitions to be out-of-operating hours or all support representatives are logged out, the system proactively routes conversations to configured fallback options such as voicemail, callback, or alternative queues. Organizations benefit from reduced wait times and lower abandonment, improved customer satisfaction during peak load or unexpected staffing gaps, and a more predictable service experience regardless of representative availability. At the same time, this eliminates the need for manual queue draining or extended shifts, helping protect service representative wellbeing while maintaining consistent service levels. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users GA date: October CY2026 Preview date: June CY2026

The orchestration can select the tool execution sequence and can include more tool calls than are required. title_original: Visual Studio Code 1.142 — Copilot / Chat / Agents
excerpt_original:
Agents
Copilot harness
The Copilot harness is powered by the Copilot SDK, a shared foundation that helps align behavior, capabilities, and improvements across Copilot products. In VS Code, the Copilot harness runs sessions through the Agent Host , which lets sessions continue in the background and be accessed from both the VS Code editor window and the Agents window.
The Copilot harness has been available from the harness picker in the chat input. Based on overwhelmingly positive and valuable feedback, we're progressively rolling it out as the default harness for new sessions in VS Code. When you start a new session, Copilot in the harness picker indicates that the session will use the Copilot harness.

Thank you to everyone who has shared feedback. We're actively using it to shape the experience. One example is reintroducing Ask as a built-in agent in the Copilot harness. Your feedback showed that a dedicated read-only experience remains valuable. Select Ask from the agent picker to use it.
Learn how to work with the Copilot harness , or explore the architecture and workflows in the agent host blog post . If you have feedback or requests, please file an issue .
Canvases (Preview)
Setting : chat.canvases.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders
Canvases are interactive interfaces to collaborate with an agent. A canvas opens beside the chat, where you and the agent can inspect and update the same artifact instead of coordinating solely through prompts.
For example, use a Kanban canvas to plan and track implementation work. You can create and move cards directly, while the agent can break a feature into tasks, update their status, or add newly discovered work. Canvases work in both the VS Code editor window and the Agents window, and canvas extensions are also supported in the GitHub Copilot app .

Canvases are available in Preview in the VS Code desktop app for local sessions that use the Copilot harness. Enable chat.canvases.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders , and then start a new session with the Copilot harness.
Every canvas is provided by a canvas extension. To get started, you have two options:
Create a canvas extension : Enter /create-canvas in the chat input and describe the user interface you want for your project. The skill then creates a canvas extension in your workspace and opens its canvas. Install a chat plugin : For now, install a chat plugin that includes a canvas extension through the GitHub Copilot app. Then switch to VS Code and ask the agent to list the available canvases and have it open one.
After you install a canvas extension, you can also open an available canvas in the Agents window from Add Tab (+) > Canvas .
Explore and install sample canvas extensions from the community .
Learn more about canvas support in the VS Code documentation.

Move chats between folders and worktrees
Previously, if you started investigating a task in one folder and then wanted to implement it in a Git worktree, or continue in a different repository, you had to start a new chat and rebuild the context.
In the Agents window , you can now ask the agent to move the current chat to another folder or into a new Git worktree, and it keeps the conversation history intact. Changing the workspace also works for chats that already have a workspace, and the agent can isolate work in a new worktree.
Ask the agent with a natural-language prompt, for example:
Continue this task in a new Git worktree of the current repository before implementing it.
The agent finishes the current turn, moves the chat, and shows a notice when the workspace changes. Then it continues the task automatically in the new location. Edits and commands run in the new location while your original checkout stays unchanged.

The move is available for agent sessions that use the Codex harness or Codex in Interactive mode, and that contain one chat and one local folder. For prerequisites and details about which files are available in the new location, see Move a chat to another folder or worktree .
Session-scoped layout in the Agents window (Experimental)
Setting : sessions.experimental.layoutScope Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders (Agents window only)
Previously, when you switched between sessions in the Agents window, VS Code shared layout settings such as editor visibility, details, and panel visibility across sessions. If you're used to VS Code remembering the layout for each workspace, sharing the layout across sessions can be disruptive.
With the new experimental sessions.experimental.layoutScope Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders setting, you can choose how much of the layout each session remembers. Reload the window after you change the setting. It supports the following values:
session-shared (default): The current behavior. A session and its nested sessions share the same editors and selected panel views. Editor, details, and bottom panel visibility are shared across existing workspace sessions. chat-shared : A session and each of its nested sessions keep their own editors and selected panel views, while editor, details, and bottom panel visibility stay shared across existing workspace sessions. chat : A session and each of its nested sessions also keep their own editor and details composition and bottom panel visibility.
Window geometry, pane sizes, and the sidebar currently remain shared across the window.
Customize the Agents window panel layout
You can now choose how the bottom panel is aligned in the Agents window. Right-click a panel tab, select Align Panel , and choose one of the following layouts:
Center aligns the panel beneath the chat area, leaving more room for the side pane. Justify extends the panel across the full width of the window.
Your selection is saved per profile and preserved when maximizing or restoring the panel.


Chat
Quickly identify the active harness
Chat titles show the active harness name, such as Copilot or Codex , so you can identify it without opening the harness picker or hovering over the session list.

Stop background shells
In Copilot harness sessions, the background shells pill above the chat input lists the commands that the agent is still running in the background. When one of those commands is no longer useful, for example a test run that you want to restart or a command that runs longer than expected, you can stop it instead of waiting for it to finish.
Select the Background Shells pill, select a shell to open its details, and then select Stop Shell next to its command. Only that command ends, and the shell leaves the list. You can reach Stop Shell with the keyboard, and screen readers announce when the shell stops.

Stopping a shell is only available for attached shells , which the agent runs as part of its current request. Detached shells run independently of the agent and can't be stopped from this interface.
Shell details also show each shell's full description above its command, even when the list truncates it. Long output is no longer cut off, and you can scroll back through earlier output, both in the shell's details and in the terminal output in the chat response.
Stateful responses for BYOK custom endpoints
If your bring-your-own-key (BYOK) model uses a stateless Responses API, set "statefulResponses": false on its model entry in chatLanguageModels.json to send full conversation history with each request.
See Custom Endpoint configuration for details.
Windows sandboxing for Local harness is no longer supported
Windows sandboxing for terminal commands in Local agent sessions has been deprecated. For sandboxed command execution on Windows, use an Agent Host session. See the Agent Host sandboxing documentation for details.
Redesigned model picker
Copilot and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) providers offer many models, each with strengths for different tasks. The redesigned model picker makes it easier to choose and switch models as your work changes.
The model picker uses a tabbed interface to separate Copilot and BYOK models.

When you hover over a model in the list, you can further configure its thinking level and context window size.

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Commerce: Enable MCP tools for POS returns
excerpt_original: This feature provides reusable MCP tools for Store Commerce POS returns. These tools expose Commerce return capabilities as structured actions that customers, partners, and agent developers can use to build conversational or agentic return experiences. The tools enable agentic experiences to look up the original purchase using supported identifiers such as receipt, order, invoice, or confirmation number; retrieve matching transactions and returnable lines; identify items that are returnable, partially returnable, already returned, or not returnable; create a return using selected lines, quantities, and reason codes; determine eligible refund options for original-tender refund scenarios; and execute eligible original-tender refunds through existing Commerce return and payment logic. The tools can also explain return eligibility, policy restrictions, and why specific lines may or may not be returnable. They can analyze prior returns and refunds to surface duplicate-refund risk, frequent-return patterns, cross-store return history, or other return-risk indicators. Tool responses provide structured data that host experiences can use to present return details, choices, summaries, and next steps in the experience they build. Customers can use these tools from POS-embedded agents, chat-based copilots, workflow orchestrators, or other agentic surfaces. Setup is performed by an administrator, IT owner, or implementation partner. Customers configure the host surface, authorize the agent or integration to call the tools, and maintain existing Commerce return policies, reason codes, tender rules, and payment configuration. GA date: March CY2027 Preview date: October CY2026

excerpt_original: Consolidated AI settings make it easier for makers and admins to find and manage AI capabilities for model-driven apps across two complementary surfaces. Makers can see and adjust all available AI options for the app in one place instead of finding them scattered among all the other settings. In the Power Platform admin center, model-driven app AI settings are consolidated from Environment > Settings into Copilot Hub > Power Apps . This provides a central location for settings such as Generative pages, Copilot in apps, and the in-app AI skills. As part of this consolidation, the old model-driven app AI switches under Environment > Settings will also be retired and removed. title_original: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.97
excerpt_original: 2026-10-13 - Add agent-scoped declarative hooks for custom agents - Remote plugin marketplace and plugin fetches retry once with your signed-in GitHub token after HTTPS auth fails. - Streamed responses behind TLS-intercepting proxies complete when close_notify is omitted - Fix parsing of GitHub SCP remotes with absolute paths so repository owner and name resolve correctly - Discover all custom agents even when repositories define more than 100 or nest agent files deeply. - Autopilot denies a preToolUse hook's "ask" decision instead of stopping on a permission dialog nobody is watching - Keep Windows taskbar agent icons grouped across CLI updates by using a stable icon path - Keep saved settings such as dismissed prompts, trusted folders and sign-ins when one entry in config.json is invalid, instead of resetting them on every launch - In /config, managed permission rules are read-only and hidden unless set by your organization. - Show billed AI Credits in /usage for token-billed sessions, including after resume - File reads using a view_range that is not exactly two elements, such as a lone start line, now show their line range and line count in the timeline, and session exports no longer contain the literal text undefined - Dragging to select text in the transcript no longer occasionally highlights and copies the row below the pointer. - Power BI and Bluebird MCP servers accept their published resource scopes during sign-in - Redact secrets safely in --output-format json output while preserving valid variable references - Resuming suspended sessions now reports interrupted tool calls and avoids replaying canceled writes. - Synchronous /task JSON output now includes failed child error and lifecycle events before completion. - Explicit GitHub MCP tool and toolset selections use the correct endpoint, so requested write tools stay available. - Cached MCP tool calls recheck their definition when a concurrent tool-list refresh changes the catalog. - Skills and custom agents from --plugin-dir plugins now reach autocomplete and invocation instead of going missing. - Fixed resumed sessions rebuilding plugin hooks from the wrong plugin list, so hooks from repository-local marketplace plugins now keep running after `--resume`, and hooks from plugins your configuration disabled no longer come back - Keep /user switch new-session choices visible after account checks in short terminals - Unavailable permission recovery attempts are now tracked per request, so unrelated calls no longer consume each other's retry budget. - Background-shell wait status no longer animates when no foreground work is running - Emergency memory relief in long sessions can now bypass its cooldown before V8 aborts, so a session that would have been killed by a JavaScript heap out of memory crash may survive with compacted history instead - Inline images render by default on supported terminals without enabling experimental mode. Use `/settings inlineImages false` to turn them off

title_original: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — October 5
excerpt_original: This week’s updates make Copilot easier to use across accounts and environments, with more control over what agents can access and how you manage their work. GitHub Copilot Claude Haiku… The post GitHub Copilot weekly releases — October 5 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
title_ja: GitHub Copilot 週次リリース (10月5日)
summary_ja: 今週のアップデートにより、複数のアカウントや環境でCopilotが使いやすくなりました。エージェントがアクセスできる範囲や作業管理の制御が強化されています。さらに、GitHub CopilotにClaude Haikuが追加されました。

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Scheduling with Copilot
excerpt_original: Users can now schedule appointments and meetings directly from chat. Simply ask Copilot to create an appointment or schedule a meeting with colleagues, and it will find available times, book rooms, draft agendas, and send invites—all within the chat experience. GA date: October CY2026
title_ja: [提供予定・ロードマップ] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilotによるスケジュール管理機能
summary_ja: ユーザーはチャットから直接、予定や会議の作成ができるようになります。Copilotに依頼することで、空き時間の検索、会議室の予約、アジェンダのドラフト作成、招待の送信をチャット内で実行可能です。一般提供（GA）は2026年10月を予定しています。
changes: チャットからの直接的な予定および会議のスケジュール設定
空き時間の検索、会議室の予約、アジェンダ作成、招待送信の自動化

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Copilot Studio: Discover and use shared plugins in Copilot Studio
excerpt_original: Copilot Studio now connects to Microsoft's shared plugin registry, making it easier for makers to discover and use plugins, connectors, and other available capabilities. This integration provides a more consistent way to extend agents with capabilities across Microsoft's AI ecosystem. GA date: November CY2026 Preview date: October CY2026
title_ja: [提供予定・ロードマップ] Microsoft Copilot Studio: 共有プラグインの検出と利用
summary_ja: Microsoft Copilot StudioがMicrosoftの共有プラグインレジストリと接続し、メーカーがプラグインやコネクタをより簡単に発見して利用できるようになります。この統合により、MicrosoftのAIエコシステム全体でエージェントの機能を一貫した方法で拡張することが可能になります。プレビューは2026年10月、一般提供（GA）は2026年11月に予定されています。
changes: Microsoftの共有プラグインレジストリとの接続機能の追加
プラグイン、コネクタ、および利用可能な機能の発見と利用の簡易化
MicrosoftのAIエコシステム全体におけるエージェント拡張の一貫性向上

title_original: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.96-0
excerpt_original: **Improved** - Interactive sessions in git repositories reach the input prompt sooner - Timeline now shows whether you, Assisted Permissions, policy, or unattended fallback made each permission decision. **Fixed** - /add-dir grants sandbox access to added directories for the current session - /user list shows the authentication source for each signed-in account - Show retry progress messages before recovered responses after transient model failures - Model completions no longer show an authentication warning when an account-owned catalog is unavailable while signed out
title_ja: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.96-0 リリース
summary_ja: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.96-0がリリースされ、Gitリポジトリ内の対話型セッションにおける入力プロンプト表示の高速化や、パーミッション決定のタイムライン表示の改善が行われました。また、サンドボックスアクセスや認証ソースの表示、一時的なモデル障害からの回復処理に関する複数の不具合が修正されました。
changes: Gitリポジトリ内の対話型セッションで入力プロンプトに到達するまでの速度を改善
タイムラインにパーミッションの決定主体（ユーザー、Assisted Permissions、ポリシー、unattended fallback）を表示するように変更
/add-dirコマンドが現在のセッションに対して追加されたディレクトリへのサンドボックスアクセスを付与するように修正
/user listコマンドで各サインインアカウントの認証元を表示するように修正
一時的なモデル障害からの回復後に、再試行の進捗メッセージを表示するように修正

title_original: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.95
excerpt_original: 2026-10-09 - Use native Microsoft Entra broker authentication on macOS when available, with browser fallback. - copilot config supports sandbox credential injectHosts keys, with key completion in Bash, Zsh, and Fish. - --context now applies to new and resumed ACP sessions instead of silently using the default or previously saved context tier - Managed plugin setup retries hourly or after policy changes instead of on every message failure
title_ja: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.95 リリースノート
summary_ja: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.95がリリースされました。本バージョンでは、macOSにおけるネイティブなMicrosoft Entraブローカー認証のサポート、sandbox credential injectHostsキーに対応したcopilot config、およびACPセッションにおける--contextの適用動作の修正が含まれています。また、管理対象プラグインのセットアップに関するリトライ処理の改善も行われました。
changes: macOS環境で利用可能な場合に、ブラウザフォールバック付きのネイティブなMicrosoft Entraブローカー認証を使用するように変更
copilot configがsandbox credential injectHostsキーをサポートし、Bash、Zsh、Fishでのキー補完を追加
--contextフラグが、デフォルトや以前保存されたコンテキスト階層を暗黙的に使用するのではなく、新規および再開されたACPセッションに適用されるように修正
管理対象プラグインのセットアップにおけるリトライが、メッセージ失敗時ごとではなく、1時間ごとまたはポリシー変更後に実行されるように変更

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilot Chat in OneNote can create, edit, and refine content
excerpt_original: Copilot in OneNote can generate new content and directly edit when in edit mode. In this mode you can create, rename, and delete pages, sections, or notebooks as well as add or edit content in pages. changes: 編集モード時における新しいコンテンツの生成と直接編集機能の提供

title_original: Visual Studio Code 1.141 — Copilot / Chat / Agents
excerpt_original:
Agent loop
Copilot harness
The Copilot harness adds exciting new agent functionality to VS Code. It's powered by the Copilot SDK, so its behavior and capabilities are consistent with other Copilot products, including the standalone GitHub Copilot app and the Copilot CLI.
To start using the Copilot harness, select it from the harness picker in the chat input. In this release, it might already be the default selection for you. You can continue working as you normally do.

The harness runs in a dedicated agent host process based on the Agent Host Protocol (AHP), so you can connect to the same agent session from multiple VS Code windows.
Learn how to work with the Copilot harness , or explore the architecture and workflows in the agent host blog post . If you have feedback or requests, please file an issue .
Reclaim storage from inactive worktrees
Run Chat: Open Worktree Cleanup to see how much disk space inactive agent session worktrees use and remove the ones you no longer need. Filter sessions by how long they have been inactive, review each worktree's size, and select the worktrees to clean up.
The cleanup editor also lets you configure automatic cleanup for sessions with merged pull requests and control whether VS Code suggests cleanup when session storage grows large.

When chat.agentSessions.sessionStorageCleanupSuggestion.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders is enabled, the Agents window notifies you when enough inactive worktrees accumulate or they use enough disk space to make cleanup worthwhile.

Cleaning up marks the selected sessions as done and deletes their worktrees. You can restore a session later to recreate its worktree. Active, running, needs-input, and pinned sessions are protected from cleanup.
Keep track of background shells
When the agent runs a command in the background, it keeps working on other steps while the command runs. In Copilot harness sessions, a Background Shells pill above the chat input lists the shells that are still running, in both the Agents window and the editor window.
Select the pill to see each shell's command and how long it has been running, and select a shell to watch its output stream as the command runs, if output is available. A shell leaves the list when its command finishes.

More control for agent-triggered messages
When agents delegate work across conversations, they can adjust the delegated task as requirements change instead of waiting for the other session to finish. The send_message tool supports these actions between sessions and nested sessions on the same agent host:
Steer an active conversation with a correction. Queue a follow-up as a separate turn. Replace a queued message while preserving its place in the queue. Cancel a queued message before processing begins.
Queued messages run in order. After a message starts processing, it can no longer be replaced or cancelled.

Agent UX
Arrange sessions in a grid
Compare results, monitor long-running tasks, or work across related conversations without repeatedly switching between sessions. Like in the editor window, the two-dimensional session grid in the Agents window lets you drag sessions into horizontal or vertical splits and resize the panes.
Maximize a session when you need to focus, then return to the grid to continue working across conversations.

Compact layout density
Setting : window.density.layout Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders
Fit more content in the Agents window with the Compact layout density. Compact density uses a shorter title bar, removes the gaps between workbench parts, and reduces pane spacing.
By default, the Agents window follows the user-level window.density.layout Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders setting, which also applies to editor windows. To set a different density for the Agents window only, open it and choose View > Layout Density . The density of editor windows remains unchanged.

Additional session-filtering options
Focus your sessions list on the work you care about. Open Filter Sessions to filter independently by:
Environment : Where the session runs, such as locally, in the cloud, or on a remote host. Harness : Which agent harness the session uses. Created In : Which application created the session, such as VS Code, Copilot CLI, or the Copilot app.
The menu also brings together ordering, grouping, Show Done , and Created Externally controls.

Track activity across nested sessions
Nested sessions let you split related work across separate conversations. In the Agents window, each nested session shows its unread status and last-modified time, helping you find recent activity and conversations that need your attention without opening them individually.

Status is tracked independently for each conversation:
Opening a nested session marks only that conversation as read. An unread nested session does not make the main session appear unread. The last-modified time reflects activity in that conversation, not activity in the main session or another nested session.
Read status and last-modified times persist when you reload the window or restart VS Code.
To clear unread status for an entire session tree, right-click the main session and select Mark as Read . Unrelated sessions are not affected.
Simplified new-session controls (Experimental)
Settings : sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders , sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders (Agents window only)
The experimental new-session composer keeps your prompt at the center while making session choices easier to review. Workspace, repository, and harness controls now appear in a collapsible Session Options tray above the chat input.

Getting-started tips now appear in a rounded notice below the chat input, so they no longer separate the session controls from your prompt.

Collapse the tray to reduce visual clutter without changing your selections. The composer remembers your choice, adapts labels as the window narrows, and keeps the options expanded when screen reader optimized mode is active. When you use a custom chat background, the tray has an opaque surface to keep its controls readable.
Improved context picker positioning
The Add Context picker now opens next to the button that invoked it and closes when you select the button again. This keeps the picker visually connected to the chat input in the editor and Agents windows.

Move agent picker in context control (Experimental)
Setting : sessions.chat.experimental.agentsPickerInAttachContextMenu Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders (Agents window only)
If you prefer to have the Agent picker initially hidden from the chat input to reduce the number of controls, you can configure this setting to move it into the Add Context menu. After you select an agent, the picker returns to the chat input.

Customize new-session welcome messages (Experimental)
Settings : sessions.chat.experimental.welcomePhrases Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders , sessions.chat.experimental.welcomeMessages Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders (Agents window only)
New-session welcome messages add personality to the Agents window. In this release, you can add your own phrases to the defaults or replace the default phrases. Use the {name} placeholder to position your welcome name anywhere in a phrase.

Select Customize Welcome Message beside the heading to change your name or open the phrase setting. You can also right-click the heading and select Hide Welcome Message to turn welcome phrases off.

Agent environments
Continue local external Copilot sessions without reloading
New conversations from the Copilot CLI and GitHub Copilot app are now picked up automatically as external sessions as soon as you send the first request, even when the Agents window is already open. You can open and continue these conversations directly from the Agents window.

Use the Created In and Created Externally filters to choose which conversations appear in the sessions list.
Codex chat handoff between apps
Pick up a Codex chat started in the ChatGPT app or Codex CLI and continue it in VS Code's Agents window on the same machine, with your conversation history intact. You can switch back to the ChatGPT app or Codex CLI later and continue the same chat.
To use your GitHub Copilot subscription in VS Code, choose a Copilot model in the model picker. For example, you can keep working with Copilot after reaching your ChatGPT usage limit.
With Codex enabled and Created Externally sessions visible, chats created or updated in ChatGPT or Codex CLI appear within a few seconds without reloading VS Code.
Only one application can send messages to the chat at a time. If ChatGPT or Codex CLI still has the chat open, a This chat is open in another app banner in VS Code explains why sending is unavailable. Fully quit ChatGPT or exit the Codex CLI session, then select Retry . Your draft and attachments stay in place, and Retry checks access without sending your message.

Download remote files from the editor
Save an open remote file locally, without having to navigate for it in the Files panel. In the Agents window, open the editor's More Actions menu and select Download... to download the file to a local destination.
Dev Container samples (Experimental)
Setting : chat.agentHost.devContainer.samples.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders (Agents window only)
Try an agent with a ready-to-use development environment without first cloning a repository or installing its language tools locally. The Agents window now offers Dev Container samples for Go, .NET, Node.js, PHP, Python, and Rust.

Install and start Docker , and then enable the setting. Open a new session in the desktop Agents window, select Dev Container Sample from the workspace picker, and send a prompt.
This also requires chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders and chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders to be enabled.

Agent security
Sandboxing in the Copilot agent host
Settings : chat.agent.sandbox.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders
Sandboxing gives you more control over what Copilot can access while working on a task. It limits how supported agent operations access files and network resources, and helps to reduce the impact of model mistakes, prompt injection, untrusted dependencies, and locally launched tool servers.
Depending on the operation and platform, these restrictions use operating-system protections or checks within the agent host process. Sandboxing adds a layer of protection, but does not replace endpoint security or provide a standalone security boundary.
Sandboxing is available on Windows, macOS, and Linux . On Windows, required operating-system updates must be installed. Refer to Check platform availability for more details.
To configure sandboxing for all your sessions, enable the chat.agent.sandbox.enabled Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders setting. You can also control sandboxing at the session level with the Sandboxing for terminal toggle in the Permissions menu.

You can further customize filesystem permissions and network access via their respective settings in VS Code.
Sandboxing works with both local and connected remote sessions. For local sessions, restrictions are enforced on your machine. For remote sessions, they are enforced on the remote host where Copilot runs tools and commands. Filesystem permissions refer to paths on the machine running the agent.
Locally launched MCP and language servers are sandboxed by default when sandboxing is enabled.

Chat experience
Persistent progress in chat
Settings : chat.experimental.persistentProgress Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders , chat.experimental.persistentProgressVerbosity Open in VS Code Open in VS Code Insiders
Persistent progress is rolling out to all users. It keeps in-progress responses visible and lets you control how much progr

title_original: Microsoft 365 Copilot release notes — October 06, 2026
excerpt_original: Updates released between September 22, 2026, and October 06, 2026. Microsoft 365 Copilot Seamless Search and Chat Integration [Windows, Web] Microsoft 365 Chat brings the power of conversational AI directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot Search, enabling users to move effortlessly from finding information to acting on it. Search results become the foundation for contextual chat, allowing you to ask follow-up questions, synthesize insights, and generate contentâall in one unified experience. This integration reduces workflow fragmentation, accelerates decision-making, and delivers a more intuitive way to interact with your organizationâs knowledge. Roadmap ID: 512429 Details: What changed: Microsoft 365 Copilot Search now embeds conversational AI chat directly within search results. Previously, users had to switch between search and chat tools separately. This update allows follow-up questions, insight synthesis, and content generation based on search context in a unified interface, reducing workflow fragmentation. Why: Integrating chat with search streamlines user interaction with organizational knowledge, accelerating decision-making and reducing the need to switch tools. Try this: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Search. Enter a query and review the search results. Use the chat pane to ask follow-up questions or generate content based on the results. Why this matters: This integration simplifies workflows by combining search and chat, helping users act on information faster. Business impact: Teams experience faster decision cycles and less disruption from switching between search and chat applications. Personal impact: You save time by accessing search results and conversational AI in one place, reducing task switching. Regenerate response for alternative answers [Web] The Regenerate action lets you quickly get an alternative response to your latest prompt using options like Try Again or Switch Model, helping you explore different answers and improve output quality. Details: What changed: Previously, users had to re-enter prompts to get different responses from Copilot. Now, the Regenerate action provides simple buttons to request alternative answers or switch AI models without starting over. This streamlines refining outputs and exploring variations. Why: This change reduces friction when iterating on AI-generated content, enabling faster exploration of ideas and improved response quality. Try this: Enter a prompt in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. At the end of Copilot's response, open the "More options" menu. Select 'Try Again' to get a new response. Choose 'Switch Model' to see answers from a different AI model. Why this matters: Quickly generating alternative responses helps users find the best information or phrasing without repeating input steps. Business impact: Teams can iterate on AI-generated content more efficiently, improving decision-making and content creation speed. Personal impact: You save time by refining outputs with fewer steps and can explore more options easily. Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility Edit query string and user identity mapping rules for Copilot connectors [Windows, Web] Admins can now edit query string and user identity mapping rules directly in connector settings without opening a support ticket. Details: What changed: Query string parameters and user identity mapping rules are now editable after a connection is created. Admins can update them in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Settings > Search & intelligence > Data sources, then select the connection and edit its configuration. Previously, these values were fixed at connection setup and changing them required support intervention. Why: Source systems change, teams re-scope projects, filters need tightening, and identity mappings drift as directory attributes are updated. Locking these rules at setup meant every adjustment became a support request, leaving connections stale or over-scoped in the interim. Try this: Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Search & intelligence > Data sources. Select your connection (for example, Azure DevOps or ServiceNow) and open its configuration. Update the query string or user identity mapping rule and save. Confirm the change took effect on the next crawl and spot-check results for an affected user. Why this matters: Access scope and content scope are now self-serve. Admins can correct a mis-scoped connection or a broken identity mapping in minutes instead of waiting on a support cycle. Business impact: Faster remediation when a connection surfaces content to the wrong audience, fewer support tickets per connection, and configuration that keeps pace with changes in the source systemâall of which support access-governance and compliance commitments. Personal impact: You fix scoping and permission-mapping issues yourself, on your own schedule, instead of filing a ticket and waiting for someone else to make a change. Microsoft 365 SharePoint Admin Center - detailed report on Everyone except external user permissions [Web] The new report provides SharePoint Advanced Management admins complete item-level details of permissions granted to special SharePoint groups: Everyone and Everyone except external users. Roadmap ID: 561038 Details: What changed: The SharePoint Admin Center now includes a detailed report that shows item-level permissions for special SharePoint groups: Everyone and Everyone except external users. Previously, admins had limited visibility into these item-level permissions. This report helps identify exactly which items have these special SharePoint groups as recipients, improving permission auditing and security management. Why: Admins need precise visibility into permissions granted to broad groups to manage access risks effectively. This report enables admins to: Audit permissions at a granular level Detect unintended access Enhance security compliance Try this: Open the SharePoint Admin Center and navigate to Advanced Management > All features > Data access governance reports. Select the new report 'Sites and files shared via special SharePoint group' and trigger the relevant report. Export the prepared report and review item-level permission details. Why this matters: Detailed permission reports help prevent unauthorized access and support compliance with organizational security policies. Business impact: Teams can better manage SharePoint permissions, reducing security risks and simplifying audits. Personal impact: Admins save time identifying and resolving permission issues with clearer, item-level insights. Learn Get item-level permission details for "Everyone except external users" and "Everyone" Generate a report on sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups PowerPoint Create custom skills in Copilot in PowerPoint [Windows] Create custom skills in Copilot in PowerPoint for tailored workflows for your specific presentation needs. Details: What changed: Copilot now supports user defined custom skills, allowing users to extend its capabilities with personalized commands and workflows in PowerPoint. Previously, Copilot operated only with built-in skills and predefined functions in PowerPoint. This update enables customization within Microsoft 365 security and compliance standards. Why: Users need more flexibility to automate unique presentation tasks and workflows. Custom skills let users: Define specific commands suited to their content style. Automate repetitive or specialized tasks. Enhance productivity by tailoring Copilot to their needs. Try this: Open PowerPoint and access the Copilot pane. Select 'Create custom skill' to define new commands. Test your custom skill within your presentation workflow. Why this matters: Custom skills let users personalize Copilot to match their unique presentation workflows, reducing manual effort. Business impact: Teams can standardize and automate specialized presentation tasks, improving consistency and efficiency. Personal impact: You save time by automating repetitive tasks and gain more control over Copilotâs assistance. Reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint [Mac] You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint. Roadmap ID: 555897 Details: What changed: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name. Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations. This update makes it easier to use relevant Microsoft 365 content without manually attaching or uploading the file. Why: This change makes it easier to create presentations using content you already have in Microsoft 365. You can naturally reference a relevant file in your prompt, and Copilot can use that file as context when creating your presentation. Try this: Open PowerPoint and start creating a presentation with Copilot. In your prompt, reference a file saved in SharePoint or OneDrive by the document name and/or owner of the document. Ask Copilot to create a presentation using information from that file. For example: âCreate a presentation summarizing the key findings from the DOCUMENT NAME.â Why this matters: You can bring existing SharePoint and OneDrive content into your presentation workflow more naturally, without first locating the file and manually attaching it. Business impact: Teams can create presentations faster by integrating cloud-stored resources without switching apps or manually uploading files. Personal impact: You save time locating and incorporating relevant files, reducing friction in presentation creation. Viva Insights Copilot Analytics - Cowork adoption and impact [Web] Deeper insights into Cowork adoption and impact, accessible from Copilot dashboard and Consumption dashboard in the Microsoft 365 services tab. Includes export capability. All metrics can be queried by analysts with the new Consumption query (credit usage data) and through the Person query (Cowork usage data) in advanced insights. Roadmap ID: 567005 Details: What changed: The Consumption dashboard and Copilot dashboard now include expanded metrics on Cowork adoption and its impact. Analysts can export data and use the new Consumption query in advanced insights to explore all metrics. Previously, such detailed analytics and export options were unavailable. title_original: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.92
excerpt_original: 2026-10-05 - Add `copilot config` subcommands to list, read, set, and remove settings. - Add a pre-conversation Ctrl+E environment picker to switch between local and cloud runs - Entra-protected MCP servers can silently renew access-token-only credentials. - Legacy HTTP+SSE MCP connections no longer hang indefinitely when a message POST is never acknowledged; the acknowledgement is bounded by the server's configured timeout - Voice runtime install errors name why the download from nuget.org failed, not only the fallback feed's 401 - Compaction keeps your latest prompt when requests exceed context limits - Large Anthropic requests rejected by provider size limits now retry after downscaling images or removing attachments - Custom agent model entries keep model-bound reasoning effort only when that model is selected - Shell tool calls now stream live stdout and stderr output reliably in the timeline - Usage reporting preserves provider-reported reasoning token totals when available - Sessions no longer slow to a crawl for minutes after the agent writes a very large file in one step - Sandboxed shells now withhold ambient GITHUB_TOKEN unless explicitly configured. - Plan usage reflects the current billing period after quota resets - Custom agents launched through ACP task calls now resolve and run correctly - Remote session resume now uses your configured GitHub auth for --resume and --connect - Entra sign-in falls back to browser auth when no broker is available and shows a manual URL when auto-open fails - `copilot sandbox ca` commands now respect `--config-dir` (including with `-C`). - Search commands avoid sandbox bypass prompts when access is already granted - Sandboxed uv commands can write to the uv cache by default when dev tool access is enabled - pnpm commands run in sandboxed sessions without lock-file permission errors - Pressing `n` repeatedly in the Sessions tab reliably creates each new session - Reverse search updates results when command history finishes loading at startup - MCP tools recover within the same turn when server instructions change - Changing experimental mode with /experimental or /settings takes effect after restart even when launched with an opposing experimental flag - Keyboard, paste, and mouse input now stay ordered and responsive during rapid interaction. - Sandboxed shell commands offer a network bypass prompt whenever the proxy blocks a destination - Sandboxed scripts that run Git now authenticate with masked credentials and SSH remote rewrites - Sub-agents keep working after you replace your GitHub authentication credentials - Sandboxed commands on Windows write temporary files to the granted temp directory, so tools that rename a temp file into place work - Prompt-mode sessions fire a single sessionEnd hook after Stop-hook continuations complete - Reconnect to remote MCP servers after idle Streamable HTTP sessions expire - Messaging a running background agent now steers its active turn at the next processing opportunity. - Context rollovers keep your latest requests in the recovery context. - Hide the automatic sandbox CA setup prompt on Windows accounts that cannot self-elevate - Copilot no longer describes a subagent as configured when the current session cannot run it. Previously a session that could not use rubber-duck still reported it as set up in /subagents, and asking for it failed instead of being skipped cleanly. - MCP tools continue working after OAuth reauthentication when tool definitions are unchanged - Select which account to use after Microsoft Entra sign-in, and let /logout sign out those OAuth sessions. - Improve first-run startup by extracting the bundled CLI package in a child process - Improve startup responsiveness when connecting many MCP servers at once - Canvas actions can now return images to the model in invoke_canvas_action. - Remove retired models from the model picker and supported CLI selections

title_original: [Roadmap] Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Use Dataverse Business Skills in Sales Agent
excerpt_original: Business Skills are natural language instructions authored and stored in Microsoft Dataverse that teach Sales Agent how work gets done within a specific organization. Business Skills enable organizations to create natural language instructions for Sales Agent to follow, which represent their business processes, policies, and business knowledge. Business skills can represent common sales workflows such as lead qualification, pipeline reviews, account planning, opportunity scoring, account brief creation, or organization-specific sales methodologies. Sales Agent uses the instructions in Business Skills to deliver responses that align with the customer's business processes and guidance. Sellers can interact with Sales agent using natural language and receive responses that are guided by their organization's Business Skills, following admin defined sales processes, applying company specific guidance, and surface insights that reflect how the organization operations. Administrators enable the required Dataverse capabilities, create and manage Business skills within Dataverse, and control Business skill access. Business skills can be authored using natural language instructions and associated with the organization's CRM environment. GA date: November CY2026 Preview date: September CY2026

One click opens a guided execution flow that delivers ready-to-use outputs (emails, documents, presentations, and more), so users can complete their unfinished work faster with higher quality. This feature will be available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium license in Edge. GA date: January CY2027 Preview date: November CY2026

title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Improve purchase order matching in Payables Agent
excerpt_original: This feature improves PO matching quality in Payables Agent and aligns draft finalization behavior with existing posting controls. The agent uses an enriched PO Lines list page during matching that includes these fields: Line Amount — enables matching on value, not just description and quantity. This field is especially valuable for service lines where quantity (often just 1) isn't a meaningful discriminator. Expected Receipt Date — helps the agent factor in timing when multiple PO lines could match. By using these fields, the agent can more reliably distinguish between similar-looking PO lines, which improves accuracy in first-pass matches. The agent now respects the app's Never block draft finalization setting in the Receipt on Invoice field on purchase orders. This change means the agent doesn't block draft finalization because a matched PO line isn't yet marked as received. Whether goods are received is a posting time control, not a draft time control. The "Receipt on Invoice" setting on the order governs this behavior at posting. The "Receipt on Invoice" field is already available on purchase orders. With this release, we're expanding this setting to more entities: A new vendor-level "Receipt on Invoice" setting is introduced and automatically applied to new purchase orders created for a vendor. A new PO-line-level "Receipt on Invoice" setting allows per-line override. The inheritance chain for the setting is vendor, then purchase order, and then purchase order line, but each level can override the parent. We've also improved draft warnings. When the agent creates a purchase invoice draft matched to a PO, the draft surfaces warnings based not just on quantity, but also on amount. The draft warnings are for information only and don't block finalization. For example, they warn about the discrepancies in the draft and you can decide how to proceed. GA date: October CY2026

Instead, agent‑generated suggestions—such as descriptions, text proposals, or field‑specific updates—appear inline where they can be evaluated and modified before being applied. By keeping the review process within the page context, users maintain flow, reduce clicks, and ensure content quality with minimal disruption. The feature builds on existing Business Central autofill user interface patterns ensuring admins and users can adopt it as part of existing agent‑powered daily workflows. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Show avatars for record creators and modifiers in list
excerpt_original: This feature introduces visual avatars in Business Central list pages to indicate which user or agent created or last modified a record. The capability enhances traceability and supports collaborative work by making identity information immediately visible without opening the record. The avatars reflect either a named Business Central user, a system user or an AI agent, following the existing identity model. Users can hover over the avatar to see a tooltip with the full display name and record update timestamp (if available). This improvement benefits roles that frequently work with shared data—including accountants, order processors, warehouse staff, service teams, and administrators—by reducing time spent verifying ownership or responsibility for items, documents, or configuration entries. It also helps organizations adopting AI‑generated records understand when an automated agent has contributed. The feature surfaces existing Created By and Modified By fields more intuitively while respecting Business Central’s data privacy and permissions model. Business Value: Supporting avatars for the users or agents who created and last modified entries makes record ownership clearer and easier to understand across Business Central. By surfacing identity information directly in list pages, you can quickly determine responsibility, follow up with the right person, and work with shared data more confidently. title_original: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Manage tasks from all agents in dedicated task pane
excerpt_original: This feature introduces a dedicated task pane in Business Central that displays all tasks generated by the agents. The task pane appears as an additional panel in the user interface and can be opened from anywhere in Business Central. Tasks include suggestions, validations, follow‑ups access to draft documents, and other agent‑initiated actions. Users can review task details, navigate directly to the affected record, complete tasks, or dismiss them. This improvement primarily benefits roles that rely heavily on AI‑driven workflows—such as accountants, sales people, and managers—who often engage with multiple agents throughout the day. The task pane reduces friction by collecting all insights in a single location, minimizing missed tasks and improving throughput. Business Value: The Show all agent tasks on a separate task pane feature help organizations get more value from Microsoft Copilot in Business Central by giving users a single, structured place to review and act on AI‑generated tasks. Instead of relying on notifications scattered across different pages, users gain a clear, consolidated overview of all tasks created by agents working in finance, purchasing, sales, and operations. excerpt_original: 2026-09-30 - Add support for GPT-6.1 Sol in model selection - Add --mcp-github-auth to scope GitHub account auth to approved MCP server origins - Add session-scoped read-only directory approvals to path access prompts - Permission prompts remain answerable after resuming interrupted sessions. - Auto-approval now takes into account messages you type while the agent is working, as it already did for prompts sent while it was idle - Compaction now returns a summary even when instructions ask for tool use. - Copying selected text on Wayland now finishes as soon as wl-copy accepts it, instead of timing out and falling back to the in-process clipboard that can print "Somebody else owns the clipboard now" over the UI - A narrow Sessions sidebar drops keyboard hints that do not fit instead of cutting one off mid-word - MCP tools recover after transient discovery failures without restarting the session; unchanged catalogs remain available during recovery. - "No supported model available" is no longer shown on launch or in the model picker when a configured provider already supplies a model - MCP tool calls complete even when servers keep sending progress updates after responding - A fresh launch no longer prints "Failed to read model provider attribution" errors while it signs in - MCP OAuth sign-in to servers such as Datadog reuses a still-valid cached token - Withdrawn running prompts stay removed after session resume - Click anywhere on expanded tool calls in compact timeline to collapse them - Holding Space and Ctrl+X V explain when voice mode is off or still getting ready
